title: A Practical Pipeline for Patient-Specific Musculoskeletal Modeling: A Comprehensive MRI-Based Framework.
abstract: Patient-specific musculoskeletal (MS) modeling can provide estimates of internal joint loading that canot be measured directly. However, limitations in automated segmentation due to data-scarce environments, morphing difficulty caused by anatomical variability, and functional non-alignment are major bottlenecks that hinder the practical application of modeling and reduce productivity in musculoskeletal research. To comprehensively address these practical issues, this study proposes and validates an integrated, automated modeling framework.. First, we automatically segmented the lower extremity bones of the 4 knee osteoarthritis patients using a multi-atlas-based segmentation algorithm. By integrating the segmented bone with motion capture and force plate data, a modeling pipeline including multi-stage morphing and functional alignment processes was implemented. Using the constructed customized model, the medial and lateral knee contact forces (FMC and FLC) were estimated during a single-leg step-up exercise, and these were compared and evaluated against the results based on manual segmentation. The contact forces estimated through the automated segmentation framework demonstrated high consistency with the manual results. The mean absolute error ranged from 0.04 ± 0.03 to 0.06 ± 0.03 BW for FMC, and from 0.06 ± 0.04 to 0.09 ± 0.07 BW for FLC, and the intraclass correlation coefficient demonstrated a high correlation of over 0.99 across all patients. This study demonstrated that the proposed automated pipeline provides a practical approach to address misalignment caused by anatomical variability, while generating joint load estimates equivalent to the manual approach. By addressing key methodological challenges, this study will bring patient-specific models closer to future clinical application, where they could help assess individual loading across different activities and inform treatment and rehabilitation strategies.

title: Parameter analysis for diffusion tensor imaging corresponding to microstructural alterations following spinal cord injury.
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is a quantitative MRI technique that enables non-invasive, in vivo evaluation of spinal cord injury (SCI). Based on the anisotropy of water molecule diffusion, DTI provides superior detection of microstructural alterations compared with conventional MRI. Diffusion is quantified by parameters including fractional anisotropy (FA), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), average diffusion coefficient (DCavg), axial diffusion (AD), radial diffusion (RD), and mean diffusion (MD), each showing distinct temporal sensitivity to SCI. Changes in these indices reflect underlying tissue disruption and are closely correlated with neurological function in both experimental and clinical studies. Despite extensive investigations, a systematic summary of their diagnostic and prognostic value has been lacking. This review highlights parameter sensitivity at different injury stages and the associated microstructural changes. AD and DCavg demonstrated high sensitivity in the acute phase, whereas FA was particularly sensitive in the chronic phase. ADC and MD showed mild sensitivity in acute and subacute stages but became more relevant chronically, while RD exhibited low sensitivity in acute phase but progressively increased over time. Collectively, DTI provides critical diagnostic information, and cross-linked analysis of multiple metrics across time points enables more accurate evaluation of SCI severity and prognosis.

title: Retrospective multi-reader evaluation of a Deep-Learning-based cancer detection model in Contrast-Enhanced Mammography.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the clinical impact of a deep-learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool applied to contrast-enhanced mammography on radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reading efficiency. Methods In this retrospective single-centre study, 150 contrast-enhanced mammography examinations were interpreted by five radiologists. Each case was read and annotated twice in two sequential sessions: first without assistance and then with the computer-aided diagnostic tool, with a minimum 4-week washout period. Diagnostic performance was assessed at lesion and breast levels using free-response receiver operating characteristic analysis, area under the curve, and false-positive rate. Reading time for one radiologist was recorded as an exploratory measure. Results The computer-aided diagnostic tool was associated with improved lesion-level performance for most radiologists, with a mean increase in the area under the free-response curve of 0.030 ± 0.018. At 89% sensitivity, false-positive findings decreased by an average of 11.4% ± 24% across all radiologists. No improvement was observed at the breast level, possibly related to the tool's single-view analysis and dataset characteristics. An exploratory analysis showed a 31% reduction in reading time for one radiologist. Conclusion Integration of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool into contrast-enhanced mammography was associated with improved lesion-level diagnostic performance and reduced false-positive findings, without measurable improvement at the breast level. Advances in knowledge To our knowledge, this study provides one of the early clinical evaluations of a deep learning-based computer-aided diagnostic tool for contrast-enhanced mammography, suggesting potential improvements in lesion-level diagnostic performance and workflow efficiency while highlighting current limitations at the breast level.

Objectives

title: Delayed diagnosis of congenital pulmonary airway malformation in an infant: diagnostic challenges and surgical implications.
abstract: Although congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) is usually diagnosed during prenatal screening, delayed presentation may increase diagnostic uncertainty and operative complexity. We report, to our knowledge, the first case of CPAM diagnosed and surgically managed in Syria in a 4-month-old infant presenting with a 1-month history of dyspnea, fever, and poor feeding in the absence of routine prenatal screening. Initial chest radiography, although technically limited, demonstrated a rounded opacity in the right hemithorax, while non-contrast chest computed tomography (CT) revealed multicystic lesions with a hyperattenuating intralesional component, raising suspicion for secondary infection or pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB). The patient underwent right upper and middle bilobectomy, and histopathological examination confirmed CPAM and excluded PPB. This case highlights the complementary roles of postnatal CT, surgery, and histopathology in confirming CPAM and excluding PPB, particularly when delayed presentation increases operative complexity.

title: Internal herniation through Petersen's defect following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass presenting as subacute bilateral lower extremity edema due to IVC compression - a case report.
abstract: A 38-year-old woman with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) 2 years prior presented to the bariatric clinic on multiple occasions with postprandial abdominal pain and bloating and bilateral lower extremity edema. Abdominal pain did not improve despite antiacid medication and dietary recommendations. Computed tomography scan of the abdomen revealed an internal hernia (IH) through Petersen's defect (a potential space between the Roux limb and transverse colon), with a mass effect on the inferior vena cava by herniated bowel. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed the diagnosis. Reduction of the hernia and defect closure resulted in full symptom resolution. This case highlights the importance of high clinical suspicion for IH in any patient with a history of RYGB and abdominal pain, even when symptoms are chronic and/or atypical. Early recognition is important for prompt treatment and prevention of bowel ischemia and necrosis.

title: Emphysematous gastritis with extensive portal venous gas and endoscopic mucosal necrosis: gastric preservation despite an alarming presentation.
abstract: Emphysematous gastritis (EG) is a rare, potentially life-threatening condition. Extensive gastric pneumatosis and portal venous gas may suggest irreversible ischemia, although radiological severity and mucosal injury do not necessarily indicate transmural necrosis. A 70-year-old man presented with acute epigastric pain and vomiting. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated extensive gastric and duodenal pneumatosis with portomesenteric venous gas but patent visceral arteries. Immediately after CT, he developed cardiac arrest, with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 14 min. Emergency laparoscopy showed a viable stomach without perforation or transmural necrosis, whereas intraoperative endoscopy demonstrated extensive necrotic-appearing gastric mucosa. Gastrectomy was therefore avoided. Follow-up CT 4 days later showed complete resolution of pneumatosis and portomesenteric venous gas. The patient subsequently died from post-anoxic neurological injury and multiorgan failure. Surgical exploration and gastric resection should remain distinct decisions in severe EG, integrating imaging, endoscopy, and direct assessment of gastric viability.

title: MRI-Based Machine Learning to Differentiate True Progression from Pseudoprogression in Glioblastoma: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. Methods PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. Results Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. Conclusions MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous.

Conclusions

MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

title: Hormone Receptor-Positive HER2-Negative Oligometastatic Breast Cancer: prognostic stratification and pattern of progression.
abstract: Background The management of oligometastatic breast cancer (OMBC) remains controversial, particularly regarding selection for local ablative treatment (LAT). In HR+/HER2- OMBC, where prolonged survival is often the case, improved stratification and characterization of progression may guide treatment. We aimed to define prognostic subsets, assess the contribution of Modern-Imaging-Methods (MIMs; 18F-FDG-PET/CT or WB-MRI) to LAT selection, and describe progression after first-line therapy in these subgroups of patients. Materials and methods All consecutive patients with HR+/HER2- OMBC treated at our institution between 2012 and 2020 were included. OMBC was defined as ≤ 5 metastases. Prognostic factors including biological subtype, anatomical distribution, imaging modality, and LAT were evaluated for overall and progression-free survival (OS, PFS). Results Among 145 patients (median follow-up 82.8 months), median OS and PFS were, respectively, 81.1 and 26.5 months. Luminal-A-like subtypes, absence of liver metastases, and use of MIMs independently predicted better survival. LAT improved PFS (hazard ratio [HR]=0.52; 95%CI[0.29-0.91], p=0.0233) and showed a trend toward longer OS. In patients staged with MIMs, LAT significantly improved both OS (HR = 0.29; 95%CI[0.12-0.73], p=0.008) and PFS (HR = 0.40; 95%CI[0.21-0.77], p=0.0064). After first-line systemic therapy, only 18% developed polymetastatic progression. Conclusion In HR+/HER2- OMBC, three actionable considerations emerge: staging must incorporate modern imaging to accurately define metastatic burden; LAT may be considered in selected patients with low-grade disease, absence of liver metastases, and long disease-free interval; in oligoprogression after first-line therapy, LAT should be re-evaluated within a multidisciplinary setting. These data offer pragmatic benchmarks to individualize treatment while awaiting definitive randomized evidence.

title: Neonatal Cardiac Tamponade Related to Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter: A Rare Case Report.
abstract: Background Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are commonly used in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) to provide prolonged intravenous access for preterm and critically ill infants. They are generally preferred over surgically placed central venous catheters because of easier insertion and, in some settings, lower infection rates. However, rare but life-threatening complications may occur. Cardiac tamponade, resulting from catheter malposition or delayed migration with perforation of the superior vena cava (SVC) or cardiac wall, is one such complication. This case highlights the need for vigilant monitoring even when initial catheter placement is confirmed as correct. Clinical findings A male infant born at 32 weeks' gestation with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) required mechanical ventilation and surfactant therapy. A PICC was inserted through the right radial vein, and radiographic assessment confirmed appropriate positioning in the SVC. The infant initially improved. On day 10 of NICU admission, he developed sudden respiratory distress, hypotonia, bradycardia, and cardiovascular collapse. Diagnosis Echocardiography demonstrated severe pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade due to SVC perforation by the PICC tip. Intervention and outcome The catheter was immediately removed, and emergency pericardiocentesis was performed. Despite aggressive resuscitation, the infant died on day 11 of life. Practice recommendations Delayed perforation can occur days after apparently correct placement. Preventive strategies should include risk-stratified catheter positioning, preference for lower SVC tip placement, routine echocardiographic surveillance especially after the first week and enhanced staff training for early recognition of warning signs. Continuous quality improvement and readiness for emergency intervention are essential to improve neonatal outcomes.

title: Open Reduction for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip in the Newborn Hip Screening Era: Changing Patient Characteristics and Surgical Strategies Without Compromising Outcomes.
abstract: Introduction Newborn hip ultrasound scan (USS) for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) has significantly reduced the number of delayed cases. However, open reduction (OR) is still required when nonsurgical treatment fails in properly screened patients, as well as in neglected and late-presenting cases. The aim of this study is to compare the clinical and radiologic outcomes of OR for DDH between screened and neglected cases. Methods Patients diagnosed with DDH and who underwent OR at a single center were included and categorized into 2 groups: Screened patients with an unsuccessful nonoperative treatment attempt (group 1), and neglected patients due to misdiagnosis or lack of USS (group 2). Comparisons were performed between groups for demographic parameters, surgical characteristics, pre- and postoperative radiographic analyses, radiologic and clinical outcome assessments, and complications. Results One hundred thirteen patients (148 hips) were included (group 1=66 and group 2=82). Group 1 had younger median age at the time of OR (11 vs. 23.2 mo, P<0.001), less IHDI grade 3-4 ratio (74% vs. 90%, P<0.001) higher medial/anterior OR ratio (55% vs. 15%, P<0.001), lower rate of concomitant femoral (35% vs. 71%, P<0.001) and pelvic osteotomy (38% vs. 78%, P<0.001) as compared with group 2. PFGD (proximal femur growth disturbance) rates were similar between the 2 groups. No difference noted for Severin grade (good to excellent result 89% vs. 92%, P=0.42), McKay (excellent result 83% vs. 77%, P=0.21), revision (9.8% vs. 6.4%, P=0.33), reoperation for implant removal (14 vs. 20, P=0.23), and for pelvic osteotomy due to residual acetabular dysplasia (6 vs. 5, P=0.58). Conclusion Early detection of DDH through USS not only reduced delayed presentations but also altered the demographic, clinical, and surgical characteristics of patients requiring OR. Despite failed initial conservative management, screened patients achieved comparable radiologic and clinical outcomes to those of unscreened patients, with similar rates of complications and residual acetabular dysplasia. These findings suggest that newborn hip USS enables less extensive surgical management without compromising outcomes. Level of evidence Level III-retrospective comparative study.

title: The Hidden Trap: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome Masking Entrapped Great Occipital Nerve-A Case of Headache Surgery.
abstract: Headache syndromes may coexist with peripheral nerve entrapment, which can obscure the true pain generator and delay effective treatment. Tolosa-Hunt syndrome is a rare, painful ophthalmoplegia syndrome characterized by unilateral orbital pain and cranial nerve palsy, often showing a marked response to corticosteroids. We report the case of a 56-year-old woman with a long history of migraine who developed recurrent right-sided orbital pain, maxillary pain, and ophthalmoplegia. She was diagnosed with Tolosa-Hunt syndrome by an experienced neurologist after skull magnetic resonance imaging and clinical evaluation. Because steroids and anti-inflammatory treatment produced only partial relief, and because she also had occipital pain with a positive Tinel sign over the greater occipital nerve, occipital neuralgia was suspected. A diagnostic block of the right greater occipital nerve provided partial improvement, after which right-sided surgical decompression of the nerve was performed. At 1-year follow-up, the patient had no residual surgical sensory deficit, no recurrent severe orbital or maxillary pain, and a marked reduction in attack frequency and intensity. Her Migraine Disability Assessment score improved from 18 to 4, and medication use decreased to sporadic use of simple analgesics and triptans. In selected patients, rare headache syndromes may coexist with occult peripheral nerve entrapment. Persistent symptoms despite appropriate medical treatment should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis and targeted evaluation for occipital neuralgia.

title: Imaging Evaluation of the Transplant Liver.
abstract: Successful management of liver transplant recipients relies on accurate imaging evaluation of the liver allograft throughout the postoperative period. This review provides a practical multimodality approach to imaging evaluation of the transplant liver, highlighting the complementary roles of ultrasound with Doppler, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, multidetector computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, and selected nuclear medicine studies. Normal postoperative anatomy and expected imaging findings are reviewed, followed by a review of the characteristic imaging features of common vascular, biliary, and parenchymal complications. The strengths, limitations, and appropriate clinical applications of each imaging modality are discussed to facilitate accurate diagnosis and guide timely management.

title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Blinded Lung Ultrasound and Clinicians in Pulmonary Consolidations: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Bedside lung ultrasound (LUS) is an increasingly utilized technique as an adjunct to clinical history and physical examination. This study aims to assess the added value of LUS by comparing the diagnostic accuracy of a blinded sonographer's ultrasound findings against the clinical suspicion of pulmonologists and emergency physicians at admission. A prospective single-center consecutive study of hospitalized patients (n=101) with imaging-detected consolidations was conducted. Ultrasound was performed by a blinded operator unaware of the physician's diagnostic suspicions. Definitive diagnoses were established through clinical-radiologic follow-up at 12 months, biopsy, and/or microbiological studies. The pulmonologist and emergency physician correctly estimated the probability of benignity/malignancy in 88.1% and 80% of the cases, respectively, whereas the blind operator achieved a 90% accuracy rate. Combining LUS findings with pulmonologists' clinical data improved benign/malignant classification accuracy to 96%. The agreement with the definitive dichotomous diagnosis (benign/malignant), assessed through Cohen kappa, was 0.664 for pulmonologists, 0.129 for emergency physicians, and 0.747 for the ultrasonographer. Ultrasound demonstrated a sensitivity (Se) of 85% and specificity (Spe) of 92% for diagnosing cancer. For pulmonologists, Se was 65% and Spe was 96%, whereas for emergency physicians, Se was 12% and Spe was 97%. The approach to hospitalized patients with imaging-detected consolidations that achieves the highest diagnostic accuracy (96%) combines clinical suspicion with ultrasound findings. Our findings confirm the importance of LUS, particularly in suspected malignancy.

title: LDiT3D: Head and Neck Tumor Segmentation Using a 3D Latent Diffusion Transformer Model.
abstract: Objective Head and neck (H&N) tumors are among the most common cancers worldwide. However, manual annotation of H&N tumors for each patient poses a significant burden on clinicians. Therefore, developing automated and accurate methods for H&N tumor segmentation is of great clinical importance. Methods We introduce LDiT3D, a novel 3D transformer-based diffusion model designed to segment H&N tumors from 3D Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and X-ray computed tomography (CT) scans, primarily focusing on oropharyngeal tumors. LDiT3D utilizes stacked 3D vision transformer blocks to effectively capture spatial context in volumetric data. To address the high computational cost typically associated with 3D transformers, we incorporate a pre-trained autoencoder that projects the input into a lower-dimensional latent space where the diffusion process is performed more efficiently. In addition to the diffusion loss computed in latent space, a task-specific segmentation loss is introduced in pixel space to further enhance segmentation accuracy. Results Methods based on U-Net and transformer architectures were selected as reference methods. Comparative results demonstrated that the proposed LDiT3D achieved highly accurate segmentation performance, with the highest Dice Score and lowest Hausdorff distance on both public and local datasets. Moreover, LDiT3D showed a more balanced performance between Precision and Recall, as indicated by the highest Fowlkes-Mallows Score. originalAbstract:
Objective

Head and neck (H&N) tumors are among the most common cancers worldwide. However, manual annotation of H&N tumors for each patient poses a significant burden on clinicians. Therefore, developing automated and accurate methods for H&N tumor segmentation is of great clinical importance.

Methods

We introduce LDiT3D, a novel 3D transformer-based diffusion model designed to segment H&N tumors from 3D Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and X-ray computed tomography (CT) scans, primarily focusing on oropharyngeal tumors. LDiT3D utilizes stacked 3D vision transformer blocks to effectively capture spatial context in volumetric data. To address the high computational cost typically associated with 3D transformers, we incorporate a pre-trained autoencoder that projects the input into a lower-dimensional latent space where the diffusion process is performed more efficiently. In addition to the diffusion loss computed in latent space, a task-specific segmentation loss is introduced in pixel space to further enhance segmentation accuracy.

Results

Methods based on U-Net and transformer architectures were selected as reference methods. Comparative results demonstrated that the proposed LDiT3D achieved highly accurate segmentation performance, with the highest Dice Score and lowest Hausdorff distance on both public and local datasets. Moreover, LDiT3D showed a more balanced performance between Precision and Recall, as indicated by the highest Fowlkes-Mallows Score. Ablation studies further confirmed the effectiveness of the key components in the LDiT3D design.

Conclusion

LDiT3D delivers more accurate and balanced H&N tumor segmentation compared to reference methods.

Significance

These findings highlight LDiT3D's potential to improve automated H&N tumor annotation and advance medical image analysis.

title: PARDA: A Perceive-Act-Reflect-Distill Agent for Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation.
abstract: Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (SFUDA) has emerged as a critical paradigm for addressing severe domain shifts in medical image segmentation under strict data privacy constraints, where source data are inaccessible. However, existing SFUDA methods primarily rely on static, open-loop adaptation pipelines, lacking the ability to actively perceive target domain characteristics and use reflection to correct accumulated errors. Meanwhile, Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit strong generalization across modalities and anatomies, yet their high computational inference overhead and deployment constraints prevent direct adoption on clinical edge devices. In this work, we propose PARDA, a VLM-coupled closed-loop SFUDA framework for medical image segmentation. PARDA reformulates SFUDA as a closed-loop decision-making process, in which the method actively perceives target domain characteristics, acts by coordinating semantic and geometric VFMs to generate pseudo-labels, reflects on the reliability of its anatomical and structural representations to guide refinement, and finally distills the acquired adaptation knowledge into a lightweight student model. This design enables PARDA to mitigate error accumulation while preserving data privacy and inference efficiency. We conduct a comprehensive SFUDA evaluation covering 13 cross-modality domain adaptation directions and 24 anatomical targets across diverse organs and imaging modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that PARDA achieves robust and universal domain adaptation while distilling the adaptation results into a lightweight student model for resource-constrained inference.

title: Boiling Histotripsy with 1.1/3.3 MHz Dual-Frequency Inducing Long-Duration Anti-Tumor Immunity in Mice Breast Cancer.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) has a poor prognosis and high risk of recurrence and metastasis. Histotripsy is an ultrasound-guided, non-invasive, non-thermal ablation method that mechanically lyses target tissues. A boiling histotripsy (DF-MS BH) technique combining 1.1/3.3 MHz superposition with a multi-stage ultrasound pulse scheme was proposed, aiming to enhance anti-tumor immune response by optimizing pulse dose and number of treatments. A custom-designed 1.1-/3.3-MHz two-element confocal-annular array and multi-stage ultrasound pulses were used for treatment. For 6-mm-diameter tumors, the ablated volume accounted for 60-70 % of the total tumor volume. The anti-tumor immune results showed increasing pulse dose from 85 to 115 elevated DAMPs release and reduced tumor growth rate. After the first high-dose pulse treatment, the infiltration level of CD8 + T cells gradually increased and then decreased on the 7th day, which contributed to a 9-day period of tumor growth arrest. Following the second treatment, the release of danger signals was further augmented. Meanwhile, the high-level infiltration of CD8 + T cells persisted for 35 days, extending the tumor growth arrest period to 25 days and prolonging the median survival period of mice to 50 days. In addition, this treatment strategy effectively reduced the number of lung metastases, confirming its ability to enhance systemic anti-tumor immune response. Furthermore, DF-MS BH ameliorated the immunosuppressive microenvironment of TNBC through first and second enhanced treatments. Ultimately, the combination therapy of DF-MS BH and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) further suppressed tumor recurrence and metastasis.

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening for Osteonecrosis of the Jaw in Panoramic Radiographs.
abstract: Background Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) is a serious condition associated mainly with antiresorptive therapy and maxillofacial radiotherapy. As detection of its radiographic findings may facilitate patient referral, this study aimed to develop convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for ONJ screening in panoramic radiographs (OPGs). Methods A dataset of 888 ONJ-positive OPGs and 888 ONJ-negative controls was assembled and annotated using bounding boxes. The dataset was split at patient level 70-10-20 for training, validation, and testing. Multiple CNNs (ResNet18, ResNet34, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0) were trained on cropped image regions and evaluated using standard performance metrics. Performance on full OPGs (without cropping) was tested, and subgroup analysis was performed. Regions contributing to model predictions were visualised using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). Results EfficientNet-B0 performed best, with per-crop accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score of 92.24%, 89.80%, 94.69%, 94.42% and 82.05%, respectively. At 0.9 probability threshold, per-image accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score equalled 76.65%. Grad-CAM highlighted clinically relevant regions; however, differentiation from other changes in bone density was suboptimal. Conclusions Despite promising results at crop level, model performance in full OPG analysis is currently insufficient for clinical application. Further optimisation of localisation strategies and external validation are needed for reliable clinical application.

title: Computed Tomography-Derived Abdominal Aortic Calcification Independently Predicts Survival in Rectal Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Contemporary rectal cancer treatment pathways remain predominantly guided by tumour-related characteristics, including stage and histopathology, with comparatively limited objective assessment of physiological reserve for treatment planning. Aortic calcification represents a potential imaging biomarker reflecting systemic vascular disease, chronic inflammation and physiological reserve. We evaluated computed tomography (CT)-derived abdominal aortic calcification as a prognostic imaging biomarker for postoperative outcomes and long-term survival. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the prospectively maintained Australian Comprehensive Cancer Outcomes and Research Database (ACCORD) of rectal cancer patients treated between 2013 and 2022. Pre-treatment staging CT was subjected to semi-automated volumetric quantification of calcium using 3D Slicer software. Calcification volume was assessed segmentally at vertebral levels L1-L4 and at the iliac vessels. Primary outcomes were major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III) and overall survival. Cox proportional hazards modelling was performed using a prespecified parsimonious multivariable model. Results A total of 174 patients were included in the analysis. Increasing calcification burden demonstrated no statistically significant association with major postoperative complications (OR 1.09 per 1000-unit increase; 95% CI 0.99-1.19; p = 0.07). Increasing calcification independently predicted worse 5-year survival after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.17 per 1000-unit increase ([CI 1.08-1.28, p = 0.001]). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed separation between calcification groups, although dichotomised analyses did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion Aortic calcification independently predicts long-term survival following rectal cancer surgery but not short-term postoperative complications. Quantitative CT-derived calcification assessment may provide a rapid, objective imaging biomarker that reflects physiological reserve and represents a potential adjunct to future risk stratification pathways.

title: Differential Diagnosis Performance of ChatGPT in Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology.
abstract: Objective To evaluate ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) for ranked differential diagnoses in oral and maxillofacial pathology, assess image effects on diagnostic performance and examine output stability across repeated runs. Methods This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 160 biopsy-confirmed cases. Cases were evaluated using a standardised prompt under two conditions: text-only and text plus clinical photographs and/or radiographs. Each case underwent three independent runs. Performance was measured using Top-1, Top-3, Top-5 and Top-10 accuracy. Results Top-1 accuracy was 44.0% for text-only and 43.3% for text + image inputs. Accuracy increased at broader thresholds, with Top-10 accuracy reaching 80.7% and 82.9%, respectively, but no significant differences were observed between input conditions at any Top-K threshold. Top-1 performance was stable across runs, although variability was observed at broader Top-K thresholds in the text-only condition. Conclusions ChatGPT ranked the reference diagnosis first in fewer than half of cases, while broader differential lists more often included it. Images did not significantly improve accuracy, although heterogeneous and non-standardised visual inputs may have limited detection of multimodal effects. These findings support further investigation for hypothesis generation and educational use rather than clinical decision support or replacement of expert judgement and histopathological confirmation.

title: Differential Expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 in Oral Epithelial Dysplasia: An In Vitro Study to Explore Potential Malignant Transformation.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to better understand the expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 proteins in progressive and nonprogressive oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) cell lines to predict malignant transformation. Materials and methods Normal oral keratinocytes (NHOK810), nonprogressive OED (D30-mild, D25-severe), progressive OED (D20-moderate, D19-severe), and oral squamous cell carcinoma (H357, BICR31, and ORL188) were co-cultured with irradiated 3T3 fibroblasts. Western blotting was used to assess the protein expression of p53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 in these cell lines. Bootstrapping, one-way ANOVA, and subsequent post hoc analyses were performed for multiple comparisons. Results CDKN2A and NOTCH1 had low expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0008 and 0.0012) respectively relative to nonprogressive OED, indicating a negative tendency. Conversely, p53 demonstrated significantly higher expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0112) compared to nonprogressive OED, reflecting a positive trend of expression throughout disease progression. There was a significant difference in CASP8 expression between nonprogressive and progressive cell lines (p = 0.039); however, no linear pattern was observed as the disease advanced. Conclusion The current study illustrates that the high expression of p53, combined with low expression of CDKN2A and NOTCH1, may serve as helpful markers, providing a potential molecular complement to histopathology for predicting malignant transformation in OED.

title: Delayed Histiocytic Foreign Body Reaction and Granuloma Formation Following Argiform Injection for Soft Tissue Augmentation Mimicking a Lipomatous Tumor on Histopathology: A Case Report.
abstract: As cosmetic procedures gain popularity, the use of nonapproved soft-tissue fillers by unlicensed or untrained practitioners in nonmedical settings is rising. We report a rare case of a histiocytic reaction to foreign material following Argiform injection. A 31-year-old female presented with a 2 year history of an itchy and painful rash on both buttocks. The rash was initially confined to the right buttock but extended to the left several months later; it remained refractory to topical ointments. A skin punch biopsy revealed extensive adipocytic-like cells within the dermis, some of which mimicked lipoblasts. Immunohistochemistry showed the lesional cells were positive for CD68 and negative for S100 and pancytokeratin. A final diagnosis of a histiocytic reaction to foreign material was made. Following the biopsy results, the patient disclosed a history of cosmetic Argiform injections at a spa 4-5 years prior to presentation. This case demonstrates that delayed tissue reactions to Argiform can mimic lipomatous tumors, creating a significant diagnostic pitfall. Clinicopathologic correlation, including a thorough remote medical history, is critical for achieving an accurate diagnosis.

title: The risk of radiotherapy toxicity in patients with laryngeal cancer: predictive factors and radiobiological modelling.
abstract: Introduction The assessment of post-radiation toxicity and quality of life is a crucial aspect of patient care. To evaluate and predict post-irradiation toxicity in a cohort of patients with laryngeal cancer, radiobiological modelling, biological and medical indicators, dose-volume variables, and radiomics were used. Methods For the comprehensive evaluation, biological and medical factors, treatment plan doses, and radiomic features from pre-treatment CT images were analyzed using the PyRadiomics Python library. The Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) and Niemierko general equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) formalisms were applied for modelling and parameter estimation. The chi-square test assessed significance between categorical variables, while one-way ANOVA and the Spearman correlation were applied for continuous variables. All analyses were conducted using a custom Python 3.8 script. Results Significant indicators impacting post-irradiation toxicity were identified. The American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) comorbidity score, pre-treatment body weight loss, and weight loss during therapy were consistently associated with acute hematological, skin, and gastrointestinal toxicities. For late outcomes, pre-treatment weight loss, alcohol consumption, diabetes, and first symptoms emerged as significantly associated with overall and salivary gland toxicity. In addition, dose-volume parameters of the buccal mucosa, pharyngeal constrictor, and tongue correlated with acute mucositis, dysphagia, and xerostomia. Radiomic analysis revealed that larger and flatter target volumes were linked to increased toxicities, with PTV (Planning Target Volume) size strongly associated with hematological effects. The LKB model further identified parameters characterising the dose-response relationship for xerostomia, dysphagia, acute gastrointestinal toxicity, and overall acute toxicity. Conclusion The study identified significant factors influencing post-treatment health status and established LKB model parameters associated with radiation-induced complications.

The assessment of post-radiation toxicity and quality of life is a crucial aspect of patient care. To evaluate and predict post-irradiation toxicity in a cohort of patients with laryngeal cancer, radiobiological modelling, biological and medical indicators, dose-volume variables, and radiomics were used.

Methods

For the comprehensive evaluation, biological and medical factors, treatment plan doses, and radiomic features from pre-treatment CT images were analyzed using the PyRadiomics Python library. The Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) and Niemierko general equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) formalisms were applied for modelling and parameter estimation. The chi-square test assessed significance between categorical variables, while one-way ANOVA and the Spearman correlation were applied for continuous variables. All analyses were conducted using a custom Python 3.8 script.

Results

Significant indicators impacting post-irradiation toxicity were identified. The American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) comorbidity score, pre-treatment body weight loss, and weight loss during therapy were consistently associated with acute hematological, skin, and gastrointestinal toxicities. For late outcomes, pre-treatment weight loss, alcohol consumption, diabetes, and first symptoms emerged as significantly associated with overall and salivary gland toxicity. In addition, dose-volume parameters of the buccal mucosa, pharyngeal constrictor, and tongue correlated with acute mucositis, dysphagia, and xerostomia. Radiomic analysis revealed that larger and flatter target volumes were linked to increased toxicities, with PTV (Planning Target Volume) size strongly associated with hematological effects. The LKB model further identified parameters characterising the dose-response relationship for xerostomia, dysphagia, acute gastrointestinal toxicity, and overall acute toxicity.

Conclusion

The study identified significant factors influencing post-treatment health status and established LKB model parameters associated with radiation-induced complications.

title: Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence in Pre-Implant Radiographic Imaging: A Structured Qualitative Synthesis of Performance Across Imaging Modalities and AI Architectures.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate contemporary evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) applied to radiographic imaging for pre-implant dental assessment and treatment planning, with emphasis on the distinction between technical algorithmic performance and clinically oriented planning outcomes. Materials and methods Peer-reviewed original studies published from January 2021 through December 2025 were identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, JSTOR, and supplementary searches. Eligible studies used radiographic imaging as an integral input to AI for pre-implant assessment, planning, decision support, virtual positioning, or outcome prediction. Reporting completeness was assessed with CLAIM 2024. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-3 for eligible diagnostic/test-accuracy studies, PROBAST+AI for the prognostic prediction-model study, and RoB 2 for the randomized clinical study. Owing to heterogeneity, findings were synthesized qualitatively. Results Thirty-six studies were included. CBCT was the predominant modality. Applications included anatomical detection and segmentation, bone assessment, decision support, implant-position prediction, automated virtual placement, workflow integration, and preoperative outcome prediction. Segmentation and anatomical-analysis studies generally reported high task-specific performance, while clinically oriented positional accuracy and planning outcomes were more variable. AI frequently reduced workflow time. QUADAS-3 was applicable to five studies; four had high overall risk of bias and one unclear risk. The prognostic prediction-model and randomized clinical studies also had high risk of bias under their respective tools. Conclusions AI shows greatest current support for anatomical analysis and selected workflow tasks. Evidence for autonomous implant positioning and outcome prediction remains limited and heterogeneous. Current findings support clinician-supervised integration, with further multicenter external testing, standardized clinically meaningful outcomes, reproducibility, and prospective evaluation required before broader routine implementation.

title: Rapid noncontrast MRI screening for iliac and left renal vein compression: A practical bSSFP technique.
abstract: ObjectivesTo describe a rapid, widely available, noncontrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for first-line morphologic assessment of suspected iliac and left renal vein compression in patients with symptoms potentially related to pelvic venous disorders.MethodsWe use a two-stack axial two-dimensional balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) acquisition extending from the renal hila through the iliac bifurcation. The sequence is available on major MRI platforms as TrueFISP (Siemens), FIESTA (GE), or bTFE (Philips). Typical 1.5-T parameters are TR/TE 3.0-3.8/1.5-1.9 ms, flip angle 60-80°, 5-mm slice thickness, and 1.3-1.6-mm in-plane resolution. Localized shimming is performed for each stack.ResultsThe abbreviated examination requires approximately 10 minutes of scanner time, including planning and breath-hold acquisitions. It depicts the site and degree of iliac or left renal vein compression and demonstrates collateral pathways that may support physiologic relevance. Morphologic abnormalities are interpreted in the clinical context and are not considered diagnostic of a symptomatic syndrome in isolation.ConclusionsA short bSSFP protocol can provide a practical, radiation-free gateway examination when comprehensive MR venography is unavailable or undesirable. It may facilitate appropriate referral and procedural planning, while invasive assessment, including intravascular ultrasound when stenting is contemplated, remains necessary in selected patients.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
abstract: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R 2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: A Study on Renal Artery Variations by CT Angiography and Their Clinical Importance.
abstract: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, anatomical variations, and branching patterns of the renal arteries using multiphasic computed tomography angiography (CTA), based on the modified classification proposed by Cases et al (2017). Understanding renal artery variations is essential for preoperative planning, renal transplantation, endovascular procedures, and urological interventions.Materials and MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 1220 abdominal CTA studies performed between March 2020 and June 2024. Fourteen cases were excluded according to predetermined exclusion criteria, resulting in 1206 studies being included in the final analysis (700 males, 520 females). All examinations were performed using a 128-slice CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM; syngo CT VC 40). CTA protocols included 5-mm acquisition and 1-mm reconstruction, with administration of 100-120 mL of iodinated contrast at 5-6 mL/s via an 18G antecubital cannula. Post-processing involved multiplanar reformation, volume rendering, and 3D reconstruction. Two experienced radiologists independently reviewed all studies. Renal arteries were categorized into Types A-E and Patterns I-V. "Early division" (Types B and E) and "polar branches" (Types C and D) were further grouped for analytical purposes.ResultsAmong 1206 CTA studies, Type A (normal hilar artery) was the most common in both kidneys, with a slightly higher prevalence on the right (74.29%) than on the left (67.99%). Polar branches were more frequent in the left kidney, whereas early divisions were more common in the right kidney. Pattern 1 was predominant bilaterally (RK: 85.73%; LK: 77.61%), followed by Pattern 2. Significant differences were observed between the kidneys in the distribution of Types A, C, D, and Patterns 1 and 2.ConclusionCTA provides excellent visualization of renal artery variations, enabling precise classification and improving surgical, interventional, and transplant planning. Recognition of these anatomical differences is essential for minimizing procedural complications.

title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain.
abstract: Background Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients. Methods A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole. Results Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease. Conclusion Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection.
abstract: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach. Emerging developments include novel amyloid PET tracers, improved diagnostic accuracy with SPECT/CT, multimodality imaging strategies, and enhanced assessment of systemic disease burden extending beyond the left ventricle. There is also growing interest in longitudinal monitoring, pre-symptomatic detection, and the role of artificial intelligence. Together, these advances position nuclear medicine as an essential tool for disease characterization, risk stratification, and treatment assessment.

title: Swin-WaveNet: frequency-guided boundary restoration for robust skin lesion segmentation.
abstract: Accurate skin lesion segmentation remains difficult when dermoscopic boundaries are fragmented by hair occlusion, uneven illumination, or weak local contrast. To address this problem, the authors propose Swin-WaveNet, a frequency-guided encoder-decoder that combines a Swin Transformer backbone with wavelet decomposition and selective state-space modeling. Rather than passing skip features directly to the decoder, the proposed method separates low-frequency semantic information from high-frequency details, selectively refines boundary-related responses, and suppresses artifact-induced activation prior to feature reconstruction. The main results are reported as the mean and standard deviation of the sample over three runs. Swin-WaveNet achieved a Dice score of 89.69% ± 0.51% and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of [Formula: see text] pixels on the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) 2018 dataset. Without fine-tuning on ISIC 2017, it obtained a Dice score of 91.69% ± 1.36% and an HD95 of [Formula: see text] pixels. On Kvasir-SEG, the model achieved a Dice score of 91.63% ± 0.57% and an HD95 of [Formula: see text] pixels. In a single-run component ablation, the complete model improved the Dice score by 0.96 percentage points and reduced HD95 by 1.16 pixels relative to the internal baseline. These results indicate that frequency-selective feature processing can help preserve weak or interrupted lesion boundaries.

title: Late-onset hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction in a childhood cancer survivor treated with cranial irradiation.
abstract: Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction is a well-recognized late complication in childhood cancer survivors (CCSs) treated with cranial irradiation. We report a 42-year-old male with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed at 5 years of age and treated with chemotherapy and 26 Gray whole-brain irradiation. He presented with right upper extremity paresis due to bilateral chronic subdural hematomas. Following burr-hole drainage for the left chronic subdural hematoma, he developed anorexia, fatigue, and hyponatremia and was referred to the endocrinology department. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated hypothalamic adrenal insufficiency, severe adult growth hormone deficiency, mild gonadal dysfunction, and mixed hypothyroidism. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a suprasellar arachnoid cyst with compression of the pituitary gland. To our knowledge, this represents one of the longest reported intervals between childhood cancer treatment and the diagnosis of hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, which became clinically apparent 37 years after treatment following a prolonged asymptomatic period. This case suggests that hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction may remain clinically silent and gradually progress for decades before becoming unmasked by the physiological stress, highlighting the need for prolonged, potentially lifelong, endocrine surveillance in CCS.

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Combined With Biopsy for the Preoperative Diagnosis of a Rare Pelvic Schwannoma: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Primary pelvic schwannomas are rare and often misdiagnosed due to non-specific imaging features. Accurate preoperative evaluation remains a challenge. The clinical utility of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with time-intensity curve (TIC) analysis and targeted biopsy was evaluated for the preoperative diagnosis and management of a pelvic schwannoma. CASE REPORT A 66-year-old man presented with dysuria and lumbago. Imaging revealed a large, mixed cystic-solid pelvic mass. Conventional ultrasound demonstrated a predominantly cystic-solid lesion with limited Doppler flow, whereas CEUS showed progressive dendritic enhancement of the viable solid component from the periphery toward the center, with non-enhancement of cystic or necrotic areas. TIC analysis demonstrated a distinctive "equal-in and slow-out" perfusion pattern, supported by quantitative parameters (rise time, time to peak, fall time, and washout area under the curve). Based on these perfusion characteristics, ultrasound-guided biopsy was directed toward hyperenhanced viable regions while avoiding necrotic zones, thereby improving tissue sampling accuracy. Immunohistochemistry confirmed S-100 and SOX-10 positivity, establishing a definitive diagnosis. Complete surgical resection with bladder defect repair was performed. Postoperatively, urinary function recovered, and no recurrent urinary or pelvic symptoms were reported during outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Quantitative CEUS-TIC analysis combined with targeted biopsy provides an effective preoperative diagnostic strategy for pelvic schwannomas. The observed CEUS-TIC perfusion pattern may correspond to the heterogeneous microvascular distribution of Antoni A and Antoni B regions; however, this hypothesis requires validation in future imaging-pathology correlation studies.

title: Umbilical cord blood miR-125b-5p: a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
abstract: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) is a common respiratory disease. This study aimed to detect the expression of miR-125b-5p in the umbilical cord blood of NRDS patients and to evaluate its diagnostic and prognostic value. Fluorescence-based real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction was used to detect miR-125b-5p expression in the umbilical cord blood of NRDS patients and controls. The correlation between miR-125b-5p expression and NRDS clinical data was analyzed. Survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox regression identified risk factors for adverse outcomes, and the ROC curve evaluated diagnostic and prognostic accuracy. The level of miR-125b-5p in NRDS patients was higher than that in controls. High miR-125b-5p expression was correlated with C-reactive protein levels, umbilical artery blood gas parameters, and the lung ultrasound score. Patients with high miR-125b-5p expression had significantly shorter event-free survival (HR 2.358, 95%CI 1.345-4.133, p<0.05) and long-term survival (HR 2.489, 95%CI 1.201-5.161, p<0.05). Cox regression identified high miR-125b-5p expression, high lung ultrasound score, high PaCO₂, and high PaO₂ as prognostic factors. Umbilical cord blood miR-125b-5p is highly expressed in NRDS. It may serve as a biomarker for the diagnosis and prognosis of NRDS.

title: Seven Novel Sonographic Signs
abstract: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch. The SFH Sign for advanced cervical insufficiency and the Gentle Wave Sign for the tardus-parvus waveform are proposed for the first time in this paper. Collectively, these seven signs span the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, echocardiography, and obstetric ultrasound. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Core Muscle Injury: A Combined Orthopaedic and General Surgery Algorithmic Approach for Diagnosis, Imaging, and Treatment.
abstract: » Core muscle injury (CMI) is a common cause of groin pain in athletes and reflects pathology of the inguinal canal, rectus abdominis-adductor longus (RA-AL) aponeurosis, and pubic symphysis. » There is a substantial lack of consensus on terminology and diagnostic criteria for CMI, hindering standardized evaluation, management, and research initiatives. » Diagnosis relies on structured history, physical examinations, and provocative maneuvers to identify CMI and concurrent pathology, and fluid-sensitive pelvic magnetic resonance imaging to characterize RA-AL injury. » Treatment strategies differ across sports medicine physicians, general surgeons, and orthopaedic surgeons, underscoring the need for early cross-departmental referrals to ensure all contributing pathologies are comprehensively identified and addressed. » When both adductor/RA-AL aponeurosis and inguinal canal/abdominal wall pathologies are present, prioritizing collaborative cases between orthopaedic and general surgeons is essential for decreasing operating room time, streamlining rehabilitation, and optimizing return-to-sport outcomes.

title: Enhancing Structural Quality in Medical X-ray Super-Resolution via Domain-Aware Loss
abstract: Abstract Upscaling medical X-ray images is more challenging than enhancing natural images, because preserving accurate structural and boundary information is more important for diagnostic correctness than producing a realistic appearance. Super-resolution methods such as SRGAN, ESRGAN, and the Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT) perform well on natural images, but when applied to medical images they can cause texture hallucination, obscure anatomical boundaries, and remove clinically important features. This study presents a comprehensive comparison of four approaches: standard SRGAN, standard ESRGAN with VGG-based perceptual loss, HAT with L1 loss, and the proposed optimised models ESRGAN_USELoss and HAT_USELoss, which incorporate a domain-specific loss function designed for X-ray imaging. The proposed USELoss (U-Net, Sobel and Edge Loss) replaces the computationally heavy VGG19 perceptual loss with a lightweight U-Net encoder that preserves multi-scale anatomical structures, and adds a Sobel-based edge loss to improve boundary accuracy, prioritising diagnostic fidelity over perceptual sharpness. On the PadChest X-ray dataset the quantitative results show large gains: standard ESRGAN reaches only 22.21 dB PSNR, whereas ESRGAN_USELoss reaches 34.04 dB, while HAT_USELoss achieves the best SSIM (0.9215) and LPIPS (0.1607). The proposed methods improve edge-preservation metrics by 5.5%, demonstrating that domain-specific loss functions are effective for clinically reliable medical image super-resolution. https://github.com/1aryantyagi/Segmentation-Paper is the Github repository of the code.

title: Oral Foregut Duplicate cyst presenting as tongue-tie in a pediatric patient: a clinicopathologic case report
abstract: Abstract Oral foregut duplication cysts (OFDCs) are rare congenital anomalies arising from abnormal foregut development during embryogenesis, characterized by ectopic gastrointestinal or respiratory epithelium within the oral cavity. We present the case of a 6-year-old boy referred to with a presumptive diagnosis of ankyloglossia ("tongue-tie") who was found to have a well-circumscribed midline cystic mass within the intrinsic muscles of the tongue. MRI demonstrated a homogeneous T2-hyperintense, T1-isointense lesion with increased diffusivity and minimal wall enhancement. The mass was excised via a ventral tongue approach and delivered intact. Histopathologic examination revealed a cyst wall lined by ciliated respiratory-type epithelium with an underlying smooth muscular layer, consistent with an oral foregut duplication cyst. The differential diagnosis, including ranula, leiomyoma, rhabdomyoma, and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor, is discussed. This case highlights the importance of considering foregut duplication cysts in the differential diagnosis of congenital tongue masses, particularly when clinical presentation mimics ankyloglossia. Complete surgical excision is curative, with a low risk of recurrence.

title: Reproducibility-Aware Evaluation of Hierarchical Multiple- Instance Learning for Patient-Level Thrombosis Detection from Compression Ultrasound
abstract: Abstract Background To provide a reproducibility-aware evaluation of multi-site cine multiple-instance learning (MS-CineMIL) versus a fixed 8-frame imaging baseline under patient-level five-fold cross-validation, and to examine whether the nominal ROC AUC difference reproduces after field completion and runtime environment control. The study delineates aggregation applicability boundaries rather than presupposing a stable advantage. Methods The public ThrombUS+ Dataset #1 Training Set (v1.0; 594 subjects, 2,341 DICOM cine clips) was used. Thrombosis is a per-site label, so the patient-level endpoint was defined as engineering-positive: raw Thrombosis = 1 for any record of the same SubjectID (81/594). After quality control, 2,327 cines were retained. Partitions used SubjectID isolation. Primary metric: ROC AUC; secondary: PR AUC, Brier score. Model differences were tested by 10,000-resample patient-level paired bootstrap (empirical two-sided P values; Bonferroni α = 0.0167). Results In the V1 historical frozen analysis, the ROC AUC difference of MS-CineMIL versus the fixed 8-frame baseline was + 0.0740 (95% CI 0.0043 to 0.1454, P = 0.039), failing Bonferroni correction. In the same-environment controlled comparison, the difference was − 0.0283 (95% CI − 0.1177 to 0.0608, P = 0.538) with a larger Brier error (+ 0.0374, P < 0.001). The baseline re-run yielded 0.6390; the complete model ROC AUC was 0.6419. The between-run baseline shift (0.0711) matched the nominal gain (+ 0.0740); no stable advantage emerged. Conclusions The V1 frozen difference did not pass multiple-comparison correction, was not reproduced under controlled comparison, and was accompanied by a larger Brier error. Evidence supports boundary auditing of model components, field completeness, and aggregation strategies, but not stable superiority, clinical deployment, external applicability, or novelty claims.

title: Adenosquamous carcinoma of the colon with an aberrant MLH1 immunostaining pattern: a diagnostic pitfall in mismatch repair assessment
abstract: Abstract Background Adenosquamous carcinoma (ASC) is a rare histological subtype of colorectal cancer (CRC) that carries a poor prognosis and has been associated with a distinct molecular profile - higher frequency of mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR), PD-L1 overexpression, and KRAS mutations. With recent advances in CRC therapeutics, molecular characterization of rare histological subtypes has become increasingly important. Here, we report a case of colorectal ASC with a distinctive dMMR immunohistochemical profile and provide a review of the literature on this rare colorectal neoplasm. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 64-year-old woman who presented with a three-month history of worsening abdominal pain and recent-onset hematochezia. Abdominal CT revealed a large mass involving the right colon. She underwent a total pelvic exenteration. Histopathology showed a high-grade, poorly differentiated tumor with mixed glandular and squamous components, staged as pT4b pN1a. Immunohistochemistry confirmed both glandular and squamous differentiation. Mismatch repair protein analysis showed loss of PMS2 expression and a granular, dot-like MLH1 staining pattern—interpreted as loss of expression and consistent with a known clone-specific artifact—while MSH2 and MSH6 were retained, supporting a dMMR phenotype. The patient received mFLOX chemotherapy but died four months postoperatively due to disease-related complications. Discussion This case illustrates the classic clinicopathological features of ASC, alongside a dMMR immunoprofile that may carry therapeutic relevance given the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in MSI-high colorectal tumors. The findings also underscore the importance of correctly recognizing clone-specific MLH1 staining artifacts, as misinterpretation could falsely suggest isolated PMS2 loss and trigger unnecessary germline testing for Lynch syndrome. Given the rarity of ASC and its limited molecular characterization, accurate MMR status assessment remains critical for guiding treatment decisions and avoiding diagnostic pitfalls.

Mismatch repair protein analysis showed loss of PMS2 expression and a granular, dot-like MLH1 staining pattern—interpreted as loss of expression and consistent with a known clone-specific artifact—while MSH2 and MSH6 were retained, supporting a dMMR phenotype. The patient received mFLOX chemotherapy but died four months postoperatively due to disease-related complications. Discussion This case illustrates the classic clinicopathological features of ASC, alongside a dMMR immunoprofile that may carry therapeutic relevance given the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in MSI-high colorectal tumors. The findings also underscore the importance of correctly recognizing clone-specific MLH1 staining artifacts, as misinterpretation could falsely suggest isolated PMS2 loss and trigger unnecessary germline testing for Lynch syndrome. Given the rarity of ASC and its limited molecular characterization, accurate MMR status assessment remains critical for guiding treatment decisions and avoiding diagnostic pitfalls.

title: Contour-free multi-instance learning versus conventional CT features for preoperative Ki-67 stratification in gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors: a retrospective comparison
abstract: Abstract Background : Manual tumor contouring adds a separate preprocessing step to CT-based prediction. We therefore evaluated whether complete-series multiinstance learning (MIL) could perform preoperative Ki-67 stratification from dual-phase CT without tumor contours and provide greater discrimination than conventional CT features. Methods : This retrospective study included 61 patients. Ki-67 cutoffs of 5%, 8%, and 10% defined three cutoff-specific tasks. Patients whose reported Ki-67 interval spanned a cutoff were excluded only from the corresponding task. Twenty-one conventional variables were analyzed with two conventional models, and frozen ResNet-18 features from the complete arterial and venous phase series were analyzed separately with five MIL methods. Four prespecified equal-logit fusion combinations were evaluated. Patient-level stratified fivefold cross-validation was repeated 10 times. Assessment comprised AUROC, AUPRC, calibration assessment, decision-curve analysis, paired bootstrap comparisons with Holm correction, and a post-training attention audit. Results : The three tasks included 59, 54, and 56 patients, with 41, 26, and 15 positive cases. The highest AUROCs were 0.645 (95% CI, 0.485–0.781) at 5%, 0.646 (95% CI, 0.496–0.788) at 8%, and 0.605 (95% CI, 0.442–0.753) at 10%. The maximum AUPRCs at 5%, 8%, and 10% were 0.822, 0.637, and 0.346. Every AUROC confidence interval included 0.5, and no comparison among the prespecified individual models or between fusion and its components remained significant after Holm correction. In the attention audit, 34 of 60 tests remained significant after global Holm correction, with 21 estimates above and 13 below their prespecified references. Conclusions : Complete-series MIL was applied separately to arterial and venous CT series for cutoff-specific Ki-67 stratification and did not require tumor contour inputs. It showed no clear discrimination advantage over conventional CT features in this cohort. External validation and direct assessment of annotation burden are required before clinical use.

title: Correlation between Serum MMP-1/TIMP-1 Ratio and the Severity of Diabetic Retinopathy in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of blindness among the working-age population. Current screening and grading primarily rely on fundus imaging, lacking serological markers that reflect early molecular pathological changes. There is an urgent need to identify biomarkers for early warning and progression assessment of DR. Purpose To investigate the correlation between serum levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, TIMP-1, and their ratios with the severity of DR in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), providing serological references for early identification and risk assessment of DR progression. Methods and Results Sixty-four T2DM patients were enrolled and divided into three groups based on fundus findings: Non DR group (n = 31), non-proliferative DR (NPDR) group (n = 17), and proliferative DR (PDR) group (n = 16). Serum levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, and TIMP-1 were measured using ELISA, and the MMP-1/TIMP-1 and MMP-2/TIMP-1 ratios were calculated. Results showed that serum MMP-1 levels and the MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio exhibited an increasing trend across the three groups and were significantly positively correlated with DR severity grading (r = 0.283, P = 0.023; r = 0.344, P = 0.005). No statistically significant differences were observed in MMP-2, TIMP-1 levels, or the MMP-2/TIMP-1 ratio among the groups, nor were they significantly correlated with DR severity. Conclusion Serum MMP-1 levels and the MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio increase with the severity of DR and may serve as novel serological candidate markers for reflecting DR progression. The MMP-1/TIMP-1 ratio showed a stronger correlation than the single marker, suggesting its potential value as a comprehensive indicator of extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation and remodeling balance in assessing DR progression. Future studies with larger sample sizes and combined ocular local samples are needed for further validation.

title: Interpretable Concept-Bottleneck Vision-Language Model Predicts Pathologic Complete Response From Longitudinal Breast DCE-MRI
abstract: Abstract Deep learning can predict neoadjuvant treatment response in breast cancer, but most models are black boxes whose reasoning clinicians cannot verify, limiting adoption. We developed an interpretable concept-bottleneck vision-language model (CB-VLM) that predicts pathologic complete response (pCR) from pre-treatment and early-treatment dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI, routing every prediction through eleven radiologist-recognizable, BI-RADS-style imaging concepts plus age and molecular subtype. Trained on 753 patients from the multicenter I-SPY2 trial, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.76 on encoder-held-out data (n = 144) and generalized to an independent I-SPY1 cohort (AUC 0.71; n = 110). Accuracy rose with model confidence (88% versus 58% on borderline predictions), and early change in functional tumor volume was the dominant predictor across both cohorts. To our knowledge, this is the first large vision-language model to generate concept-grounded reasoning for breast DCE-MRI treatment response prediction, reframing a black-box task as transparent, auditable, and generalizable.

title: Thenar Muscle Thickness Assessed by Point-of-Care Ultrasound and Geriatric Vulnerability in Hospitalized Older Adults: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Malnutrition and sarcopenia frequently coexist in hospitalized older adults. Thenar muscle thickness (TMT) may provide a pragmatic correlate of geriatric vulnerability, but its clinical relevance is unestablished. Methods This retrospective, single-centre, cross-sectional pilot study analyzed 50 hospitalized patients aged 75 years or older, admitted between October and December 2024. Unadjusted Spearman correlations assessed associations between TMT and Mini Nutritional Assessment–Short Form (MNA-SF), Braden, and Conley scores. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were calculated for these three correlations. Results Mean age was 86.2 years; 60.0% of participants were women. Mean TMT was 2.62 cm (SD, 0.48). Overall, 84.0% of patients were malnourished or at risk of malnutrition, 66.0% had high pressure-injury risk, and 90.0% had a Conley score indicating fall risk. Higher TMT correlated with higher MNA-SF (rho = 0.760; 95% CI, 0.595–0.859; P < 0.001) and Braden scores (rho = 0.560; 95% CI, 0.340–0.729; P < 0.001), and with lower Conley scores (Rho = − 0.406; 95% CI, − 0.627 to − 0.141; P = 0.003). Associations remained directionally consistent after adjustment for age and sex: partial rho was 0.753 (95% CI, 0.572–0.865) for MNA-SF, 0.510 (95% CI, 0.251–0.709) for Braden, and − 0.361 (95% CI, − 0.602 to − 0.054) for Conley. TMT was not significantly associated with length of stay (Rho = − 0.240; P = 0.093). Conclusions In very old hospitalized adults, lower TMT was associated with poorer nutritional status and greater fall and pressure-injury risk. TMT may complement multidimensional geriatric assessment, but the small, unadjusted pilot design and absence of a sarcopenia reference standard preclude diagnostic or independent prognostic claims.
