title: MRI-based preoperative WHO grade prediction in meningioma: development and comparison of deep learning, radiomics, clinical, and combined models in multicenter data.
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study was to develop and externally validate complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models and their stacked combinations for preoperative World Health Organization (WHO) grading of intracranial meningioma. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 455 histopathologically confirmed meningiomas: a four-center development cohort (n = 346) with leave-one-center-out cross-validation and an external cohort (n = 109). Four base models used contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI: tumor + peritumoral radiomics, an nnU-Net segmentation-based classifier, frozen DINOv3 transfer-learning features, and clinical variables. All 15 combinations were prespecified and stacked using a linear meta-learner trained on development out-of-fold predictions. Frozen models were externally evaluated without modification. Results WHO 2-3 tumors comprised 24.6% overall (112/455; development 20.5%; external 37.6%). External AUCs were 0.732 for nnU-Net, 0.703 for DINOv3, 0.645 for clinical, 0.628 for radiomics. The multimodal ensemble (nnU-Net+DINOv3+Clinical) achieved the highest external AUC (0.742), exceeding radiomics (ΔAUC +0.114, p = 0.008) but not nnU-Net (ΔAUC +0.011, p = 0.737). Compared with the clinical model, discrimination was higher but nonsignificant at the prespecified threshold (ΔAUC +0.098, p = 0.050), while reclassification improved (IDI +0.109, p < 0.001). Radiomics-containing combinations performed strongly in development but lost most discrimination externally. The multimodal ensemble had an external calibration slope of 1.32 (Brier 0.190) and net benefit above default strategies at thresholds ≥ 0.23. Conclusion The multimodal ensemble achieved the highest external AUC but did not significantly exceed nnU-Net, which was the most transportable single predictor of meningioma grade. Clinical variables did not improve discrimination but enabled interpretable feature-level attribution. Handcrafted radiomics lacked external transportability.

title: Volumetric discordance between ¹⁸F-FET-PET/MRI and MRI-based radiotherapy target volumes in high-grade glioma: a prospective pilot study (FETSMaRT).
abstract: Purpose High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited. Methods FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression. Results Median age was 60 years; 77% had glioblastoma and 60% MGMT promoter methylation. GTV discordance occurred in 17/30 patients (56.7%) and CTV discordance in 15/30 (50.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived volumes significantly exceeded MRI-based volumes for GTV (43.6 vs. 38.6 cc; p < 0.0001), CTV (119.2 vs. 110.8 cc; p = 0.0045), and PTV (171.1 vs. 159.6 cc; p = 0.0003). Larger GTV∆ and CTV∆ change values were associated with numerically shorter median time to progression, but neither association was statistically significant. Radiation treatment failures were predominantly central (60.0%). Conclusion FET-PET/MRI-derived target volumes were significantly larger than MRI-based volumes, confirming systematic underestimation of metabolically active tumor extent by anatomical MRI. While not meeting significance in this pilot study, directional CTV and GTV discordance suggests a possible association with progression; the hypothesis generating exploratory pilot data nonetheless justify a prospective trial of FET-PET-guided RT in high-grade glioma. NCT06499831.

title: A two-stage model combining clinical and delta-radiomics features for prognosis in high-grade gliomas after chemoradiotherapy: a retrospective study.
abstract: Objective This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of integrating pre-radiotherapy and mid-radiotherapy radiomics, temporal changes in tumor radiomics (delta radiomics) during chemoradiotherapy, and clinical variables into prognostic models for individualized overall survival (OS) prediction in patients with high-grade glioma (HGG). Methods A total of 143 patients with HGG who underwent standard chemoradiotherapy were retrospectively enrolled from two centers. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 116), in which 5-fold cross-validation was performed, and an external test cohort (n = 27). Radiomics features were extracted from pre-radiotherapy and mid-radiotherapy MRI scans, and delta radiomic features were calculated as the differences between the two timepoints. Feature selection was performed using elastic-net-based stability selection, and radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were generated for each selected feature set using Cox models. Rad-scores were subsequently combined with clinical variables in a random survival forest (RSF) model for OS prediction. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was performed to evaluate prognostic stratification. Results The combined model integrating clinical variables and delta radiomics achieved a C-index of 0.818 and 0.761 in the validation and external test cohorts, respectively, outperforming models based solely on radiomics or clinical features. In the external test cohort, time-dependent discrimination yielded 12-, 18-, 24- and 30-month OS AUCs of 0.842, 0.856, 0.796, and 0.943, and Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significant risk stratification (p = 0.002). Conclusion The findings of this retrospective study suggest that integrating multi-timepoint radiomics, delta radiomics features, and clinical variables may facilitate OS prediction in patients with HGG following standard chemoradiotherapy. While promising, the exploratory findings require further validation in larger prospective cohorts, given the limited size of the external validation cohort and the absence of MGMT promoter methylation status from the main model.

title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution, while complementary multimodal, receptor-repertoire, epigenomic, and spatial approaches can link cellular states to protein phenotype, clonal architecture, regulatory programs, and tissue context. This review critically examines recent single-cell studies in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis. Rather than providing a descriptive catalogue of published studies, we assess the strength of available evidence by distinguishing independently replicated findings from observations supported by limited studies, and cross-sectional associations from longitudinal, treatment-response, and functional evidence. Across the selected diseases, studies repeatedly report inflammatory programs involving interferon signaling, chemokine-mediated immune recruitment, and stromal-immune interactions; however, evidence for convergence at the cell-state and regulatory-network levels remains limited, and the extent to which shared signatures represent common pathogenic mechanisms rather than inflammatory context remains uncertain. We evaluate the translational potential of scRNA-seq for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response prediction, while considering evidence from related tissue-based molecular stratification approaches, including the R4RA randomized trial in rheumatoid arthritis. R4RA provides prospective randomized evidence that synovial molecular features can enrich for differential therapeutic responses, but its use of bulk synovial transcriptomics and histopathology does not constitute prospective validation of single-cell-derived biomarkers. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation. Together, these advances position single-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches.

title: Neoadjuvant and Perioperative Immunotherapy for Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Current Evidence, Endpoints, and Clinical Integration.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are being investigated across curative-intent treatment pathways for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Randomized studies show that programmed cell death-1 blockade can increase pathological complete response (pCR) when added to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, while immunochemoradiotherapy can produce high pathological response rates. This structured narrative review summarizes current evidence for neoadjuvant and perioperative immunotherapy in ESCC within the context of established chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy backbones. Particular attention is given to randomized ICI trials, the role of radiotherapy, interpretation of pathological and survival endpoints, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), postoperative therapy, perioperative safety, clinical response assessment, and regional applicability. pCR is a useful early activity endpoint and may carry prognostic information within individual regimens, but definitions and pathological assessment vary and trial-level surrogacy for overall survival has not been established. Longitudinal ctDNA is promising as a complementary measure of molecular residual disease but remains investigational for treatment adaptation. When radiotherapy is combined with ICI, established thoracic organ-at-risk constraints and careful monitoring for overlapping pulmonary and esophageal toxicity remain important because ICI-specific normal-tissue constraints have not been validated. Clinical complete response assessment also requires multimodal evaluation; post-treatment inflammatory changes can limit CT and PET-CT specificity. Overall, current data support continued phase III evaluation of ICI-containing strategies with mature event-free and overall survival endpoints and with comparators appropriate to regional treatment standards.

title: Temporal patterns of the association between Achilles tendon thickening and clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention in acute and chronic coronary syndromes.
abstract: Although Achilles tendon thickening (ATT) is associated with adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whether its prognostic impact differs over time between acute (ACS) and chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 1,362 patients who underwent successful PCI and assessment of ATT using soft X-ray radiography. ATT was defined as Achilles tendon thickness ≥8.0 in men and ≥7.5 mm in women. MACE, including death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, stroke, and target vessel revascularization, were investigated for up to 3 years. To evaluate temporal differences, we conducted the Kaplan-Meier method with landmark analysis and time-segmented Cox proportional hazards analyses dividing follow-up into ≤ 1 year and 1-3 years after PCI. ATT was observed in 228 patients (16.7%), who had a significantly higher incidence of MACE compared to patients without ATT. In ACS patients (n = 387), ATT was independently associated with an increased risk of MACE within 1 year, but not beyond 1 year. Conversely, in CCS patients (n = 975), ATT was not associated with early events, but was significantly associated with increased MACE risk during 1-3 years after PCI. Similar trends were observed after excluding familial hypercholesterolemia. These findings suggest different temporal patterns in the association between ATT and MACE after PCI in patients with ACS and CCS, which may provide additional insights into risk stratification during follow-up.

title: Hospitalized primary headache in children after emergency department evaluation: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objectives To characterize the clinical features, diagnostic evaluation, management, and final diagnoses of children hospitalized for headache following emergency department (ED) evaluation, and to explore factors associated with treatment refractoriness. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 4-17 years presenting to a tertiary pediatric ED with headache as the primary complaint who required hospitalization between January 2019 and June 2024. Patients whose headache was clearly attributed to trauma, fever, or a previously identified systemic or neurological disorder were excluded. Final headache diagnoses were established during hospitalization by the pediatric neurology team, using ICHD-3 criteria when applicable. Data included demographics, clinical presentation, diagnostic testing, treatments, and discharge diagnoses. Descriptive analyses were performed, with exploratory comparisons between patients requiring ≤ 2 versus > 2 sequential pharmacologic interventions. Results Among 3,646 ED visits for headache, 162 (4.4%) resulted in hospitalization; 30 children (18.5% of admissions) had a final diagnosis of primary headache and constituted the study cohort. Mean age was 12.7 years, and 70.0% were female. Although frontal location and pressure-type pain were the most common presentation features, 76.7% of patients were ultimately diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine. Acute neurological abnormalities were documented in 10.0% of patients. Cranial CT was performed in 63.3% and brain MRI in 23.3%, with no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache identified. Intravenous metamizole (dipyrone) was the most frequently used first-line acute therapy, and 70.0% of patients required a second sequential pharmacologic intervention. Among patients diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine, 21.7% met criteria for status migrainosus. No clinical variables were significantly associated with treatment refractoriness. Conclusions Hospitalization for primary headache after pediatric ED evaluation was uncommon but identified a clinically severe subgroup, predominantly with migraine-spectrum disorders and frequently requiring escalation of acute treatment. Despite frequent neuroimaging, no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache was identified. These findings suggest that more selective imaging strategies may be appropriate in children with a reassuring clinical presentation, although prospective studies are needed to better define predictors of hospitalization, treatment refractoriness, and optimal acute management.

title: Olfactory dysfunction and limbic volumetric changes in relapsing-remitting and secondary progressive multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Objective To compare olfactory performance and olfactory-related brain region volumes between patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) and secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS) and to examine the relationship between olfactory performance and regional brain volumes. Materials and methods This prospective cross-sectional study included 65 patients with MS (43 RRMS and 22 SPMS). Olfactory function was assessed using the Sniffin' Sticks-12 Odor Identification Test. Bilateral volumes of the hippocampus, amygdala, entorhinal cortex, and insular cortex were obtained from three-dimensional T1-weighted MRI using the vol2Brain automated analysis pipeline available through the volBrain platform. Both raw and total intracranial volume (TIV)-normalized regional volumes were analyzed. For volumetric outcomes, multivariable analyses were adjusted for age, sex, and TIV, whereas analyses of olfactory performance were adjusted for age and sex. Additional sensitivity analyses incorporated disease duration and EDSS. Results In unadjusted comparisons, patients with SPMS had significantly lower Sniffin' Sticks-12 scores than those with RRMS (p = 0.004), and raw hippocampal volume was significantly lower in the SPMS group (p = 0.028). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and TIV, clinical subtype was not independently associated with hippocampal, amygdala, entorhinal cortex, or insular cortex volume (all p > 0.05). These findings remained non-significant in sensitivity analyses additionally accounting for disease duration and EDSS. The between-group difference in Sniffin' Sticks-12 scores was also attenuated after adjustment for age and sex (B = - 1.06; 95% CI, - 2.15 to 0.04; p = 0.058) and remained non-significant in further sensitivity analyses. No significant correlations were observed between Sniffin' Sticks-12 scores and regional volumetric measures. Conclusion Although patients with SPMS showed poorer olfactory performance and lower raw hippocampal volume in unadjusted comparisons, clinical subtype was not independently associated with regional brain volumes after adjustment for age, sex, and TIV, and the olfactory difference did not reach statistical significance after adjustment for age and sex. Furthermore, olfactory performance was not directly associated with regional volumetric measures, suggesting that olfactory dysfunction in MS may reflect mechanisms beyond regional structural volume alone.

title: Ultrasonography after adult living donor liver transplantation: a review of vascular and biliary complications.
abstract: Living donor liver transplantation expands access to transplantation but introduces vascular and biliary reconstructions that require specific ultrasound assessment. Ultrasonography provides repeatable bedside evaluation without ionizing radiation, allowing early recognition of impaired flow and comparison with the postoperative baseline. This review examines how graft type and reconstruction affect Doppler interpretation in adult recipients, particularly after modified right-lobe transplantation. It addresses arterial, portal venous, hepatic venous, and biliary complications, with attention to measurement technique, transient postoperative changes, and limitations of diagnostic thresholds. Contrast-enhanced ultrasonography helps resolve uncertain arterial patency and perfusion. Computed tomography, magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, and invasive studies are selected according to the suspected complication and need for treatment.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Open-Weight Large Language Models for Pathological Brain MRI Reports Classification: From Prompts to a Fine-Tuned Model.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Automated semantic classification of radiology reports can enhance clinical workflows and research, but often relies on language- and task-specific models, limiting scalability. This study aims to evaluate and improve the 0-shot baseline performance of open-weight large language models (LLMs) in the semantic classification of free-text magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports. Materials and methods A corpus of 1385 reports from a single neuroradiology center was used to assess four LLMs (GPT-OSS-20B, Magistral-Small-2509, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) of comparable scale (∼20-35B parameters). The brain MRI reports were labeled as Pathological or Non-Pathological, with the Pathological ones further classified into five diagnostic categories (Neoformation, Vascular, Inflammation/Infection, Neurodegenerative, Other). The LLMs were evaluated using zero- and few-shot prompting with majority-vote aggregation. Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) fine-tuning was then applied to the best-performing model across multiple configurations. Performance was assessed using Macro F1, Micro F1, Precision, Recall, and Exact Match Accuracy. Results The binary classification task achieved a Macro F1 score of 0.84 on the best-performing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model, while multilabel classification reached 0.81. Majority voting (MV) outperformed individual-set predictions. QLoRA fine-tuning yielded a Macro F1 score of 0.83 on the multilabel task; the improvement over the 0-shot baseline was statistically supported for Macro F1, Micro F1, Macro Precision, and Exact Match, whose bootstrap 95% confidence intervals excluded zero, but not for Macro Recall. Fine-tuning and few-shot prompting strategies are complementary, with neither consistently outperforming the other. Error analysis showed that the models struggled with borderline annotation cases and often missed secondary labels. Conclusion Open-weight LLMs demonstrate strong capability for neuroradiology report classification without extensive task-specific training. Fine-tuning further improves performance, supporting integration into scalable semantic radiology data pipelines. However, the present evidence comes from a single Italian center without external validation, and the fine-tuning gain was estimated on a small held-out test set, for which the Macro F1 improvement, though statistically significant, has a confidence interval with a lower bound close to zero. In this light, the approach is best positioned as an internal indexing and semantic-retrieval tool, supporting faster report retrieval, structured cohort identification, internal audit, and scalable phenotyping for neuroradiology research and data warehousing, as well as efficient active-learning strategies, with broader generalizability requiring additional external multicentre validation before clinical deployment.

title: Region-dependent in vivo degradation and local repair responses of a magnesium artificial lamina in a rabbit lamina defect model.
abstract: Magnesium (Mg)-based implants are promising for lamina defect reconstruction because of their biodegradability, mechanical compatibility, and bioactivity. However, in vivo degradation is usually assessed at the whole-implant level, and it remains unclear whether distinct regions of the same implant experience different degradation-repair couplings. In this study, a ZE21C Mg alloy artificial lamina was implanted in a New Zealand rabbit lumbar lamina defect reconstruction model to evaluate region-dependent degradation and local repair responses. Finite element analysis showed higher equivalent stress and strain on the residual-bone side. SEM/EDS and micro-CT analyses demonstrated the asymmetric degradation of the same implant in vivo. The residual-bone side exhibited faster Mg degradation, more severe surface and interfacial degradation, and higher TRAP-related remodeling activity, whereas the opposite side degraded more slowly, maintained a denser interface, and exhibited better bone formation and tissue integration. At 12 weeks, the remaining implant volume was 20.2 ± 2.0% on the residual-bone side, compared with 41.9 ± 5.3% on the opposite side, demonstrating pronounced region-dependent degradation within the same implant. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that rapid degradation was accompanied by stronger bone resorption and inflammatory interface reactions. The slow degradation area is associated with a more vascularized repair microenvironment that supports the matrix. These findings indicate that accelerated regional degradation does not necessarily promote bone regeneration. Therefore, region-specific degradation control may be critical for designing biodegradable Mg implants in complex anatomical environments. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Biodegradable magnesium implants are generally evaluated by their average degradation rate, despite regional differences in mechanical and biological environments. In a rabbit lamina reconstruction model, we directly compared two regions of the same ZE21C magnesium artificial lamina, limiting implant- and animal-level variability. The residual-bone side experienced higher stress, faster degradation, a less stable interface, stronger osteoclast-related activity, and poorer bone formation; the opposite side degraded more slowly and supported better tissue integration. Transcriptomic analysis linked these outcomes to distinct inflammatory, bone-resorptive, vascular, and matrix-remodeling responses. Thus, faster magnesium degradation does not necessarily improve repair. This work identifies region-specific degradation control as a key design principle for biodegradable orthopedic implants in complex anatomical environments.

title: Expert assessment of medical and organizational care for children with congenital ear malformations in the Republic of Kazakhstan: The RAND/UCLA appropriateness method.
abstract: Congenital auditory anomalies are serious conditions ranging from mild hearing loss to complete deafness, with associated speech impairment, social limitations, and disability. Our aim was to evaluate the appropriateness of medical and organizational care interventions for children with congenital ear malformations (microtia and aural atresia) in the Republic of Kazakhstan, using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Methods A nine-member multidisciplinary expert panel (otorhinolaryngologists, audiologists, pediatricians, and otologic surgeons) rated 93 diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitation interventions using a structured 9-point appropriateness scale across two rounds of evaluation. Consensus was defined as a numerical IQR (Q3-Q1) ≤2 score points combined with ≥75% of ratings within the same category. Appropriateness categories were defined as: Appropriate (median 7-9), Uncertain (4-6), and Inappropriate (1-3). Results Of 93 rated interventions, 43 (46%) reached consensus as Appropriate, 45 (48%) were classified as Uncertain, and 5 (5%) as Inappropriate. Highest appropriateness was assigned to multidisciplinary diagnostic consultations (ENT specialist, audiologist, otologic surgeon) and imaging (high-resolution CT of the temporal bones, MRI). For bilateral aural atresia, bone conduction devices were rated as Appropriate (mean 7.55-7.66). Non-intervention approaches received the lowest ratings (mean 1.11-3.00), indicating strong expert consensus against expectant management. Key organizational barriers were included as explicitly rated items in the questionnaire (items 85-93, Section 4-5 of Appendix A). Delayed or absent patient registration and follow-up (item 86, mean 8.00, median 8, Appropriate) and inadequacies in regulatory frameworks (item 87, mean 7.22, median 7, Appropriate†) were among the highest-rated organizational items, while insufficient funding (item 88, mean 6.22, median 6, Uncertain without consensus) did not reach consensus. Conclusion This first application of the RAND/UCLA method in Kazakhstan to evaluate care for children with congenital ear malformations identified clear areas of expert consensus and uncertainty. The results support the development of multidisciplinary care pathways and targeted rehabilitation policies. Findings represent structured expert opinion from nine specialist panelists in Kazakhstan and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, or national representativeness.

title: The type of portal vein reconstruction does not affect the outcomes of pancreatic surgery or the patency of the portal vein.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the safety of the four types of portal vein reconstruction (PVR) as defined by the International Study Group of Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) and to analyse long-term survival outcomes in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Methods A prospectively collected pancreatic surgery registry that was supplemented retrospectively was used. Patients who underwent open pancreatic resection with PVR between 2005 and 2024 were included. Clinicopathological characteristics, outcomes, and computed tomography images were analysed and tested in multivariate and survival analyses. For survival analyses, patients with PDAC who underwent pancreatectomy without PVR served as controls. Results Pancreatectomies with PVR (n=386) comprised 63 tangential resections with venorrhaphy (ISGPS type I), 25 patch reconstructions (type II), 147 end-to-end anastomoses (type III), and 151 resections with graft interposition (type IV). Most type IV reconstructions (98.7%) used spiral grafts, predominantly made from the great saphenous vein (GSV). PVR thrombosis rate was 3.1% at 30 days and 5.7% at 90 days following surgery. There were no significant differences between PVR types I-IV in the incidence of PVR thromboses, complications, or mortality. Median survival for PDAC patients with PVR was 22.8 months, with no survival differences between types I-IV, compared with 31.7 months in patients without PVR, p=.003. Conclusions In this setting, where PVR was performed using GSV spiral grafts for interposition, the type of PVR did not associate with pancreatic surgery outcomes or portal vein patency. The rate of PVR thrombosis was low, and other complication rates and long-term survival outcomes were comparable with international standards.

title: Orbitocranial resection for treatment of lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension.
abstract: Objectives This study reports our experience with multidisciplinary surgical management of lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension using the orbitocranial approach. Methods We reviewed treatment strategies and surgical approaches for lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension and present 2 illustrative patients who underwent orbitocranial resection at our institution in 2015. Clinical records, radiographic images, histologic sections, and archived pathology specimens were reviewed. Results Both patients underwent orbitocranial tumor resection, followed by postoperative chemoradiotherapy. Orbital reconstruction was performed using a temporalis fascia flap and split calvarial bone grafts, with split-thickness skin grafting to line the orbital cavity. The follow-up periods were 69- and 66-months, respectively. Both patients remained alive without evidence of disease recurrence during follow-up. Conclusions The orbitocranial approach, combined with postoperative chemoradiotherapy, may provide satisfactory local and regional control in selected patients with lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension. Long-term surveillance remains important because patients may remain at risk for disease recurrence or distant metastasis.

title: Segment Anything Models for medical image segmentation: From native capabilities to clinical requirements.
abstract: Medical image segmentation is essential for computer-aided diagnosis and precision medicine, yet conventional supervised models depend heavily on high-quality annotations and often generalize poorly across domains. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) family offers a transferable, interactive, and extensible foundation for segmentation, but direct medical transfer remains limited by domain gaps, insufficient modeling of medical semantics and anatomy, and mismatches in high-dimensional volumetric and sequential imaging scenarios. This review critically examines the evolution and native capability boundaries of SAM, SAM 2, and SAM 3. Across generations, native capabilities expand from spatial prompting to sequential propagation and concept-level target specification, without automatically conferring medical expertise. We organize medical adaptation from three connected perspectives: model adaptation and strategy selection, task knowledge organization and utilization, and application-oriented adaptation. Cross-method analysis shows that no strategy is universally optimal; effectiveness depends on the gap between foundation-model capabilities and target-task requirements, together with data scale, domain discrepancy, imaging dimensionality, computational resources, and clinical constraints. We further identify four priorities for clinical translation: standardized evaluation for cross-study comparability, controlled continual adaptation under clinical domain drift, dynamic resource scheduling for high-dimensional and real-time workflows, and uncertainty stratification and clinical reliability control. Overall, further progress depends on accurate capability assessment, condition-matched adaptation, and explicit control of computational and prediction risks.

title: When is 4 Gy enough? Defining dose sufficiency and durable control in indolent B-cell lymphoma.
abstract: Ultra-low-dose radiotherapy, most commonly delivered as 4 Gy in two fractions (2 Gy × 2), is an established low-burden approach for radiosensitive indolent B-cell lymphoma. Its use as stand-alone definitive local therapy is constrained by a persistent gap between early tumor regression and durable local control. This review examines when 4 Gy should be considered sufficient by integrating clinical intent, lesion biology, response assessment, immune context, and emerging biomarkers. We distinguish its use as stand-alone local treatment, palliation, response-adapted de-escalation, and immune-integrated strategies. Across these settings, early response indicates radiosensitivity but does not prove lesion sterilization or equivalence to standard-dose radiotherapy. Dose sufficiency depends on durable in-field control, tumor burden, anatomical definition, reassessment reliability, feasibility of salvage, and the consequences of local failure. Immune and cellular combinations may extend the value of 4 Gy beyond local cytoreduction, but the contribution of irradiation should be tested separately from systemic or intratumoral partners. PET response, MRD, ctDNA, and immune correlates may help distinguish transient cytoreduction from durable clearance and local response from patient-level disease control. At present, these biomarkers are better suited to trial design and mechanistic validation than to routine dose selection. Future studies should move beyond response rates and define decision rules that link early response, immune modulation, biomarker dynamics, lesion-level durability, salvageability, and cumulative treatment burden.

title: Effectiveness of technology-enabled teleophthalmology and emerging retinal imaging techniques for diabetic retinopathy screening: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes and causes preventable visual loss. Technology-enabled screening can extend retinal assessment beyond specialist settings and strengthen screening, referral, and follow-up across diabetes care pathways. Methods We systematically reviewed randomized and non-randomized implementation studies, diagnostic-accuracy and comparative retinal-imaging studies, and economic evaluations of technology-enabled DR screening. PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 23 May 2026 without language restriction. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analyses synthesized comparative and proportional outcomes, and GRADE assessed certainty. Results Thirty-three studies were included. Teleophthalmology increased DR screening uptake/completion versus usual care or pre-implementation practice (RR 1.966, 95% CI 1.451-2.664; I 2 = 75.2%) and improved adherence to recommended eye care (OR 2.464, 95% CI 1.477-4.112; I 2 = 66.47%). The pooled ungradable-image rate was 7.4% (95% CI 3.0%-17.1%; I 2 = 59.17%). Advanced retinal imaging showed pooled sensitivity of 97.59% (95% CI 94.50%-100.00%; I 2 = 0%) and specificity of 91.22% (95% CI 78.46%-100.00%; I 2 = 88.7%) for prespecified vascular lesion detection. OCTA demonstrated a pooled eye-level retinal neovascularization detection yield of 63.6% (95% CI 49.9%-75.4%; I 2 = 46.29%). Economic evaluations supported cost-effective or cost-saving technology-enabled screening across assessed health systems. Conclusion Technology-enabled DR care improves screening participation, adherence, and health-system efficiency, supporting integration of teleophthalmology and advanced imaging into scalable diabetes complication-management pathways.

title: Background parenchymal enhancement in ultrafast MRI: Inter-reader agreement before and after training, and correlations with prognostic factors of breast cancer.
abstract: Purpose To assess the inter-reader agreement in background parenchymal enhancement (BPE) categorization on ultrafast dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI before and after training and its relationship with breast cancer prognostic factors. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed the cases of 220 patients (median, age 60 years; 220 breast cancers) who underwent ultrafast DCE MRI. BPE was qualitatively classified as minimal, mild, moderate, or marked by three readers: Reader1 (R1), a radiology resident in the second year of training; Reader2 (R2), an experienced general radiologist with 28 years of experience in diagnostic radiology; and Reader3 (R3), an experienced breast radiologist with 25 years of experience in breast MRI. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated using weighted kappa (κ) values and was reassessed between R1 and R3 after intensive training. Associations between BPE levels and prognostic factors were also evaluated. Results Inter-reader agreement was substantial with weighted κ values of 0.679-0.742 for R1 versus R2, 0.612-0.665 for R1 versus R3, and 0.626-0.689 for R2 versus R3. Agreement between R1 and R3 improved slightly after training but remained substantial. No significant associations were observed between visual BPE classification and prognostic factors, including hormone receptor status, HER2 status, and proliferation markers. Conclusion Inter-reader agreement for BPE assessment on ultrafast DCE MRI was substantial and improved slightly after training. No significant relationship was observed between ultrafast BPE and breast cancer prognostic factors.

title: An integrated pathological-radiological downstaging score for prognostic classification in gastric cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: A multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) followed by surgery is the standard treatment for locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). However, post-therapy staging based on ypTNM mainly reflects residual pathological status and does not capture pretreatment disease burden or the extent of tumor regression after NAC, limiting postoperative prognostic stratification. To address this limitation, we developed a Pathological-Radiological Integrated Model (PRIM) that combines baseline stage, post-treatment pathology, and radiologic response. Methods We enrolled 414 patients with LAGC who underwent radical gastrectomy after NAC, including 348 in a development cohort and 66 in an external validation cohort. A Down-stage System (DS) was constructed to quantify tumor stage changes after NAC by weighting cT/cN and ypT/ypN categories using multivariable Cox regression. DS was then combined with RECIST response to establish the PRIM system. Prognostic performance and clinical utility were evaluated and compared with conventional ypTNM staging. Results PRIM stratified patients into four distinct risk groups with significantly different 3-year overall survival rates (86.9%, 69.9%, 40.0%, 21.2%; P < 0.001). Compared with ypTNM, PRIM demonstrated improved prognostic performance, with a higher C-index (0.728 vs. 0.696, P < 0.001), AUC (0.775 vs. 0.731, P < 0.001), and better model fit (AIC: 1471.62 vs. 1509.33; BIC: 1474.61 vs. 1512.32). Risk reclassification was also improved (NRI 14.49%; IDI 8.9%). Time-dependent ROC analysis showed consistently higher predictive accuracy for PRIM over 5 years. Conclusion By integrating pathological and radiological response information, the PRIM classification provides improved postoperative prognostic stratification compared with ypTNM alone in patients with LAGC treated with NAC.

title: Dysregulated Retinal DPP10 Expression with Single Cell-based Next Genomic Sequencing Profiling in X-linked Juvenile Retinoschisis.
abstract: X-linked juvenile retinoschisis (XLRS) is a hereditary retinal dystrophy resulting from mutations in the retinoschisin (RS1) gene, which lead to progressive structural abnormalities in the retina and consequent visual impairment. Despite this, the molecular mechanisms through which RS1 mutations induce cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling during disease progression remain inadequately elucidated. To delineate transcriptional changes associated with RS1 mutations, we conducted single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on a CRISPR/Cas9-engineered Rs1 emR209C knock-in mouse model. Integrative analysis with the Mouse Retina Cell Atlas demonstrated that rod photoreceptors exhibited the most significant transcriptional dysregulation among retinal cell types. Notably, dipeptidyl peptidase-like protein 10 (DPP10) was progressively and markedly upregulated, predominantly within photoreceptors, as the disease advanced. These findings were corroborated by immunofluorescence staining, quantitative PCR, and western blot analyses, which confirmed increased retinal DPP10 expression concurrent with a gradual decline in RS1 levels. To explore the functional implications of DPP10 dysregulation, we developed Y79 retinal cell models expressing either wild-type RS1 or the XLRS-associated RS1 R209C variant. Cells expressing the RS1 R209C mutation exhibited elevated DPP10 expression alongside reduced viability. Crucially, siRNA-mediated knockdown of DPP10 partially rescued cell viability and was associated with reduced GRP78/BiP expression in RS1 R209C-expressing cells, supporting potential functional relevance between DPP10 upregulation and mutant RS1-induced cellular stress. Furthermore, circulating DPP10 concentrations were significantly increased in patients with XLRS compared to control subjects. Collectively, these results identify DPP10 as a molecular alteration associated with RS1 mutation and suggest its potential as a circulating biomarker candidate for XLRS.

title: Joint associations of endometrial thickness and pattern with live birth after fresh and frozen-thawed embryo transfer: a retrospective cohort study of 45,729 cycles.
abstract: Objective To investigate how endometrial thickness and pattern jointly relate to live birth in fresh and frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles. Design Retrospective cohort study. Subjects A total of 45,729 embryo transfer cycles performed between January 2018 and August 2022, including 16,566 fresh and 29,163 frozen-thawed cycles. Exposure Endometrial thickness and pattern were assessed by transvaginal ultrasound on the trigger day in fresh cycles and on the day of progesterone initiation in frozen-thawed cycles. Fresh and frozen-thawed cycles were analyzed separately. Main outcome measures Live birth per embryo transfer cycle. title: Profile and classification of invasive fungal disease in patients with haematologic malignancies using microscopy, culture, biomarkers and polymerase chain reaction.
abstract: Background Invasive fungal diseases (IFDs) are significant causes of morbidity and mortality in patients with haematologic malignancies (HM). This study aimed to classify IFD using integrated diagnostic methods according to European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) criteria. Methods A prospective observational study was conducted in 100 adult HM patients not on antifungal prophylaxis. Diagnosis included microscopy, culture, galactomannan (GM) enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), Candida mannan immunoglobulin M (IgM) lateral flow assay (LFA), Aspergillus IgM assay, cryptococcal antigen LFA, (1,3)-β-D-glucan (BDG) assay and panfungal polymerase chain reaction (PCR), along with high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). Results Probable IFD was observed in 51%, possible in 24%, proven in 12% and no IFD in 13%. Acute leukaemia predominated, with invasive aspergillosis (IA) and candidiasis being the most common infections. Fever was the most frequent presentation, while respiratory symptoms were associated with invasive aspergillosis. PCR showed the highest sensitivity (88.8%), followed by BDG (87.3%). Microscopy and culture were positive in 25% cases, Aspergillus fumigatus being the most common isolate. HRCT was normal in 56%, with ground-glass opacities and consolidation as the most frequent abnormalities. Conclusion Integrated diagnostic approaches improve classification and early detection of IFD in HM patients and support timely antifungal management.

title: Is technical difficulty associated with the accuracy of patient-specific implants for maxillary repositioning in minimally invasive orthognathic surgery?
abstract: The use of patient-specific implants (PSIs) in minimally invasive orthognathic surgery remains limited due to concerns about technical difficulty and restricted intraoperative exposure. Whether increasing maxillary movement technical difficulty compromises the accuracy of PSI-assisted minimally invasive surgery remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the accuracy of maxillary repositioning using PSIs in minimally invasive bimaxillary orthognathic surgery and its relationship to technical difficulty. Consecutive patients treated at the University of Texas Health San Antonio between June 2023 and September 2025 were included if they underwent bimaxillary minimally invasive orthognathic surgery with complete preoperative and postoperative cone-beam computed tomography records. Patients with craniofacial syndromes, comorbidities affecting postsurgical healing, or those undergoing single-jaw surgery were excluded. Technical difficulty was defined by the presence of maxillary advancement >7 mm, maxillary segmentation, or posterior maxillary impaction >1.5 mm. Accuracy was measured as the root mean square linear discrepancy between planned and postoperative maxillary positions. Demographic characteristics and malocclusion type were recorded as covariates. Thirty-six patients were included, with a mean age of 27 years. Comparisons were made across advancement magnitude, segmentation status, and posterior impaction. No statistically significant differences in root mean square discrepancies were observed across landmarks or axes after correction for multiple comparisons, with the lowest observed probability value being 0.02. These findings demonstrate that PSI-assisted minimally invasive orthognathic surgery achieves clinically acceptable accuracy across varying levels of technical difficulty, supporting its reliable use even in technically demanding cases.

title: Adjunct rim plating for selected pilon fracture patterns: Lessons from hyperextension tibial plateau fractures.
abstract: Background Pilon fractures frequently involve small anterior or anterolateral marginal fragments that are susceptible to shear displacement and may not be reliably controlled by conventional periarticular plates. Rim plating is a fragment-specific, low-profile juxta-articular buttress technique that has demonstrated favorable biomechanical and clinical results in selected tibial plateau fracture patterns. This review examines the rationale for extending this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns. Methods We performed a narrative review of clinical, cadaveric, and biomechanical studies describing rim-based constructs in tibial plateau fractures, with emphasis on hyperextension and posterolateral patterns, as well as computed tomography (CT)-based studies of pilon fracture morphology and fragment capture by precontoured plates. Relevant studies were identified through PubMed and reference screening and synthesized qualitatively to inform a technical proposal for adjunct rim plating in selected pilon fractures. Results The reviewed tibial plateau literature consistently identified peripheral regions that may remain unsupported by conventional periarticular plates, particularly in hyperextension and posterolateral fracture patterns, where adjunct rim plating has been associated with maintained reduction and favorable clinical outcomes. In the distal tibia, CT-based studies suggest that commonly used anatomically precontoured plates may not reliably capture the anterolateral (Tillaux-Chaput) fragment when fragment height is less than 15 mm. In this setting, an adjunct rim plate may serve as a peripheral buttress to improve support of the articular margin, distribute subchondral stress, and prevent displacement of the articular block. Conclusions Rim plating may be best conceptualized as a joint-line buttress strategy for improving peripheral containment of shear-dominant marginal fragments. Extrapolation of this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns is mechanically plausible and supported indirectly by CT-based fragment-capture data. This technique may be useful in carefully selected anterior or anterolateral distal tibial rim fractures that are not adequately controlled by standard periarticular plating.

title: Advancing early detection of Alzheimer's disease: from established biomarkers to future innovations.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a major form of dementia, imposes an escalating global burden on public health and social care. Pathological changes in AD occur years before clinical symptoms, defining a prolonged preclinical phase. Currently, there is no effective treatment exist for late-stage AD, making early diagnosis and intervention indispensable, in which biomarkers play a pivotal role. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) biomarkers improved AD diagnostic accuracy, their clinical application is limited by invasiveness, high costs. Advances in ultrasensitive immunoassay technologies has rendered peripheral blood biomarkers easily accessible, cost-effective, minimally invasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, offering noval opportunities for AD screening, diagnosis and progression tracking. Additionally, non-invasive body fluids including saliva, urine and tears are being explored as potential biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multimodal fusion, integrated with large-scale multimodal computing frameworks, significantly improve the accuracy of early AD diagnosis. Recent studies have identified a series of promising synaptic and neuronal biomarkers, such as neurofilament light chain (NFL), neurogranin (Ng), β-secretase 1 (BACE1) and synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25). Inflammatory mediators and genetic factors also contribute to AD pathological evaluation. This review systematically characterizes biomarker profiles of emerging non-invasive carriers (saliva, urine and tears). It further synthesizes cohort-derived quantitative diagnostic metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) of multimodal AD biomarkers and conducts head-to-head comparison to clarify their respective strengths and translational limitations, aiming to provide evidence-based insights for optimizing early AD screening and diagnostic strategies.

title: [Atypical presentation of ocular syphilis].
abstract: We report the case of a 55-year-old man who presented with a sudden decrease in visual acuity in the left eye, revealing ocular syphilis associated with asymptomatic neurosyphilis. Ophthalmological examination showed mild anterior uveitis of the left eye associated with focal peripheral retinitis displaying a ground-glass appearance, multiple creamy-white superficial retinal precipitates, and obliterative retinal arteritis. Multimodal imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography (OCT), demonstrated full-thickness retinal involvement with retinal layer disorganization, retrohyaloid inflammatory deposits, and hyperreflective preretinal inflammatory condensations. The infectious workup revealed positive syphilis serology (TPHA and VDRL), while HIV serology was negative. An anterior chamber paracentesis excluded other infectious causes. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis confirmed asymptomatic neurosyphilis in the absence of neurological symptoms and with a normal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan. Treatment with intravenous penicillin G (24 million units per day for 14 days), combined with corticosteroid therapy, resulted in a favorable outcome, with regression of inflammatory signs and clinical improvement. This case illustrates an unusual presentation of ocular syphilis characterized by ground-glass retinitis associated with retinal vasculitis and superficial retinal precipitates. It highlights the value of multimodal imaging, particularly OCT, in facilitating early diagnosis and emphasizes the importance of systematically investigating neurosyphilis, even in the absence of neurological manifestations.

title: Spleen stiffness to rule out high-risk varices in advanced chronic liver disease: an individual patient data meta-analysis.
abstract: Background & aims Management of esophageal varices (EV) is of critical importance in compensated advanced chronic liver disease. We conducted an individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis to (i) investigate the performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM)-based algorithms using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) to rule out high-risk varices (HRV); (ii) develop a new model for diagnosing any grade EV. Methods We systematically searched databases for studies reporting endoscopy and SSM-VCTE data in adult patients, collecting their IPD. The main outcome was ruling out HRV. The tested algorithms were: i) Baveno-VI criteria, liver stiffness measurement (LSM) <20 kPa and platelet count (PLT) >150x10 9 /L); ii) SSM ≤40 kPa; iii) combined Baveno-SSM criteria ≤40 kPa in patients outside Baveno VI criteria. We developed and internally validated logistic regression models to diagnose any grade EV. Results Twenty studies comprising 2257 patients were included, with a summary HRV prevalence of 25%. The Baveno VI algorithm showed 100% (95%-CI:97-100%) sensitivity and 100% (95%-CI:95-100%) NPV; the rate of spared endoscopies was 17% (95%-CI:15-18%). The combined Baveno VI-SSM criteria performed best for ruling out HRV: 97% (95%-CI:94-99%) sensitivity, 98% (95%-CI:96-99%) NPV and rate of spared endoscopies of 35% (95%-CI: 34-38%). These results were robust in all sensitivity analyses, including patients with non-viral etiology (n=637) and studies using the 100 Hz module. We developed new logistic models with excellent accuracy for the diagnosis of EV, but the ability to identify patients at low risk (<10%) of EV was limited. Conclusion This large, multicenter, international study validated spleen stiffness measurement as an accurate tool to assess high-risk esophageal varices. The combined Baveno-SSM algorithm performed best in ruling out HRV. Impact and implications Spleen stiffness has been recommended to rule out high-risk varices, but the evidence supporting its use is of low-quality. Our individual patient data meta-analysis, which included more than 2200 patients with compensated cirrhosis, showed that spleen stiffness ≤40 kPa can rule out high-risk varices with a very low rate of false negatives. Its combination with Baveno VI criteria was the most efficient triage strategy, doubling the rate of endoscopies that could be safely avoided compared to using the Baveno VI criteria alone. The findings of our study strengthen the level of evidence supporting the use of spleen stiffness as an additional screening tool for high-risk varices.

Methods

We systematically searched databases for studies reporting endoscopy and SSM-VCTE data in adult patients, collecting their IPD. The main outcome was ruling out HRV. The tested algorithms were: i) Baveno-VI criteria, liver stiffness measurement (LSM) <20 kPa and platelet count (PLT) >150x109/L); ii) SSM ≤40 kPa; iii) combined Baveno-SSM criteria ≤40 kPa in patients outside Baveno VI criteria. We developed and internally validated logistic regression models to diagnose any grade EV.

Results

Twenty studies comprising 2257 patients were included, with a summary HRV prevalence of 25%. The Baveno VI algorithm showed 100% (95%-CI:97-100%) sensitivity and 100% (95%-CI:95-100%) NPV; the rate of spared endoscopies was 17% (95%-CI:15-18%). The combined Baveno VI-SSM criteria performed best for ruling out HRV: 97% (95%-CI:94-99%) sensitivity, 98% (95%-CI:96-99%) NPV and rate of spared endoscopies of 35% (95%-CI: 34-38%). These results were robust in all sensitivity analyses, including patients with non-viral etiology (n=637) and studies using the 100 Hz module. We developed new logistic models with excellent accuracy for the diagnosis of EV, but the ability to identify patients at low risk (<10%) of EV was limited.

Conclusion

This large, multicenter, international study validated spleen stiffness measurement as an accurate tool to assess high-risk esophageal varices. The combined Baveno-SSM algorithm performed best in ruling out HRV.

Impact and implications

Spleen stiffness has been recommended to rule out high-risk varices, but the evidence supporting its use is of low-quality. Our individual patient data meta-analysis, which included more than 2200 patients with compensated cirrhosis, showed that spleen stiffness ≤40 kPa can rule out high-risk varices with a very low rate of false negatives. Its combination with Baveno VI criteria was the most efficient triage strategy, doubling the rate of endoscopies that could be safely avoided compared to using the Baveno VI criteria alone. The findings of our study strengthen the level of evidence supporting the use of spleen stiffness as an additional screening tool for high-risk varices.

title: Accuracy of Diagnostic Methods for Peripheral Trigeminal Nerve Injuries: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy following oral and maxillofacial procedures may cause persistent neurosensory disturbances and neuropathic pain, yet the diagnostic performance of the available assessment methods remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated the accuracy of diagnostic methods used to detect peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries in the maxillary and mandibular regions after oral and maxillofacial procedures. PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Diagnostic accuracy and observational studies evaluating clinical, neurophysiological, or imaging-based methods for peripheral trigeminal nerve injuries were included, while non-English and nonhuman studies, reports lacking relevant diagnostic performance data, studies outside the maxillary or mandibular regions, and nonoriginal research were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2. The search identified 2914 records, of which 10 studies (0.3%) were included in the final synthesis, comprising n = 520 participants and k = 514 injured or evaluated nerves. The included studies comprised 5 prospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 retrospective diagnostic accuracy studies, 2 case-control diagnostic accuracy studies, and one cross-sectional observational study. Clinical neurosensory testing showed 96% accuracy, 100% sensitivity, 62.5% specificity, 95% positive predictive value (PPV), and 100% negative predictive value (NPV) for lingual nerve (LN) injuries, compared with 73% accuracy, 85% sensitivity, 47% specificity, 77% PPV, and 60% NPV for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. The tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic field laterality index showed 95.7% accuracy, 92.3% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, and 90.9% NPV for LN injury. Clinical neurosensory testing was widely used but had variable diagnostic performance, with lower values for inferior alveolar nerve injuries. Quantitative sensory testing and neurophysiological methods provided more balanced diagnostic profiles, especially when combined. Magnetic resonance neurography demonstrated high specificity but variable sensitivity, with greater clinical value for high-fgrade injuries. The highest single-test accuracy was reported for tongue somatosensory evoked magnetic fields in LN injury. Overall, these findings support a multimodal diagnostic approach when objective confirmation, injury grading, anatomical localization, or treatment planning is required.

title: Diagnostic Value of Tc-99m-HDP SPECT/CT in Temporomandibular Joint Osteoarthritis: Correlation with Clinical and Structural Findings.
abstract: Background This study evaluated the diagnostic utility of quantitative Tc-99m-hydroxydiphosphonate (HDP) bone single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) in temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ OA) by analyzing correlations among tracer uptake, clinical features, and structural imaging to detect early metabolically active disease. Methods A retrospective review included 48 patients (96 TMJs) with TMJ discomfort who underwent SPECT/CT and conventional imaging. Clinical parameters included pain duration, visual analog scale (VAS) score, joint sounds, mandibular range of motion, and occlusal findings. Radiography assessed condylar morphology and cortical erosion, and a Destructive Change Index (DCI) quantified bony changes. SPECT/CT uptake was expressed as maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax). Correlation and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. Results SPECT/CT uptake strongly correlated with condylar cortical erosion on CT (r = 0.80) and moderately with lateral pole tenderness (r = 0.51) and pain VAS score (r = 0.40). Joint sounds and condylar morphology correlated weakly (r = 0.26 and 0.21, respectively), while other clinical factors had negligible associations. ROC analysis identified an optimal SUVmax cutoff of 3.88, yielding 91% sensitivity (95% CI: 80-97%) and 85% specificity (95% CI: 73-94%) for detecting cortical erosion. SPECT/CT revealed increased metabolic uptake in some radiographically normal joints, suggesting the possibility of early osteoarthritic change before overt structural abnormalities became apparent. Conclusion Quantitative SPECT/CT provides complementary metabolic information beyond structural imaging and may facilitate the detection of metabolically active TMJ osteoarthritis.

Methods

A retrospective review included 48 patients (96 TMJs) with TMJ discomfort who underwent SPECT/CT and conventional imaging. Clinical parameters included pain duration, visual analog scale (VAS) score, joint sounds, mandibular range of motion, and occlusal findings. Radiography assessed condylar morphology and cortical erosion, and a Destructive Change Index (DCI) quantified bony changes. SPECT/CT uptake was expressed as maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax). Correlation and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed.

SPECT/CT uptake strongly correlated with condylar cortical erosion on CT (r = 0.80) and moderately with lateral pole tenderness (r = 0.51) and pain VAS score (r = 0.40).
